G: I’m working on an experiment for the science
fair. This is the third time I’ve failed!
B: Don’t get discouraged! Have you ever heard of
the 147/805 rule? It can encourage you to keep
trying after you fail.
G: I’ve never heard of it. Can you tell me what it
is? __________________________________________________
B: Sure. Each number represents the number of
times a great scientist failed before making a
great scientific achievement. 147 is the number
of
times
Thomas
Edison
failed
before
he
invented the light bulb.
G: Wow! That’s a lot!
B: Well, don’t be too surprised yet. The Wright
brothers tried 805 times before they finally had
success flying an airplane. In short, inventors
have achieved great things after many failures.
G: I didn’t know those great inventors went through
so much trial and error. Now I’m not afraid to
try again and again!

I'd find it hard to believe it.
I’d be very interested to know.
I'd love to hear more about it.
I'd like to know more about it.
solution: 과학 박람회를 위한 실험에서 세 번째 실패해 기분이 좋지 않은 유미에게 소년이 낙담하지 말라고 말하며 147/805 규칙이 계 속 도전하는 데 도움이 될 것이라고 했고, 이에 대해 유미가 들 어본 적이 없다고 답하며 그것에 대해 말해달라고 요청했으며, 이어서 소년이 그것은 위대한 과학자들이 과학적 업적을 이루 기까지 실패한 횟수를 나타낸다고 상세히 설명해 주고 있으므 로, 소년이 언급한 147/805에 대해 유미가 궁금증이나 호기심 을 보인 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 어떤 놀라운 사실에 대해 알게 된 뒤 그것이 믿기 어려울 것이라고 반응하는 표현인 ❷ ‘나는 그것을 믿기 어려울 것 같아.’는 빈칸에 알맞지 않다.

body:
In Alberta, Canada, there were some “aurora
chasers” who formed an informal group online.
They would leave their homes at night and try to
get exceptional photographs of auroras. Then they
would share them with the rest of the group.
In the summer of 2014, the group members
__________________________________. There were unusual
ribbons of green and purple light, some of which
seemed to stretch for thousands of kilometers.
Sometimes they lasted for just a few minutes, while
other times they remained in the sky for a whole
hour. They were similar in appearance to auroras,
yet they possessed some notably different features.
Unsure of what they were, the group decided to
name the phenomenon “Steve,” based on a scene
from an animated movie where some characters
give that name to an unfamiliar object.

body:
One evening after work, Schawinski met a friend
named Chris Lintott and complained about the
situation. Lintott suggested that he turn to the
Internet to ask other people for help. Eventually,
the two men ended up launching a crowdsourced
online project known as Galaxy Zoo. The website
was kept as (A)____________ as possible, with a very
basic design and an easy-to-use interface. This
allowed those who wanted to participate to get
started quickly. New visitors were greeted with a
brief tutorial that explained the project. Then they
were shown an image of a galaxy and asked to
click buttons that described its features. Is the
galaxy smooth and rounded? Is its shape an oval or
a spiral? After completion of the tutorial and a little
bit of practice, the participants were able to classify
galaxies effectively.
It was online media that helped spread the word
about
Galaxy
Zoo,
bringing
more
and
more
participants to the website. Shortly after the website
was launched, nearly 70,000 classifications were
being made per hour. In a year and a half, more
than 80,000 individuals participated, and they made
more than 75 million classifications. If it had not
been for those participants, Schawinski couldn’t
have classified that many images. In fact, it would
have taken him decades on his own.
More than 15 years have passed since the project
first began in 2007. Galaxy Zoo has now grown into
Zooniverse, which is one of the most popular
platforms on the Internet for (B)____________ people
who want to participate in science projects. It is
more active than ever before, with about 2 million
registered users worldwide. It now offers a wide
range of projects in astronomy, biology, physics,
and more. If you want to get involved, you should
definitely check it out!

(A)
(B)
choices: secureprivileged
complexordinary

solution: (A) 매우 기본적인 디자인과 사용하기 쉬운 인터페이스를 가졌 으며, 참여하기를 원하는 사람들이 빠르게 시작할 수 있게 했 다는 설명이 이어지므로, 웹사이트가 최대한 단순하게 유지되 었다는 흐름이 되는 simple(간단한, 단순한)이 적절하다. (B) 대중을 참여시키는(=크라우드소싱) 온라인 프로젝트인 Galaxy Zoo의 신규 방문자들은 은하수의 분류 전에 간단한 사 용 지침의 완료와 약간의 연습을 거쳤다고 했으며, 글의 마지 막에 참여하고 싶다면 확인해 보라고 권유하고 있는 것으로 보아, 특별한 전문 지식이나 기술이 없이도 누구나 참여 가능 하다는 것을 알 수 있다. 따라서 Galaxy Zoo가 Zooniverse로 성장하여 이제는 과학 프로젝트에 참여하고 싶어 하는 일반인 들을 위한 인기 있는 플랫폼 중 하나라는 흐름이 되는 ordinary(평범한, 보통의)가 적절하다.

body:
Chasing Steve
In Alberta, Canada, there were some “aurora chasers” who formed an informal group online. They would leave their homes at night and try to get exceptional photographs of auroras. Then they would share them with the rest of the group. In the summer of 2014, the group members began to notice something strange appearing in the night sky. There were unusual ribbons of green and purple light, some of which seemed to stretch for thousands of kilometers. Sometimes they lasted for just a few minutes, while other times they remained in the sky for a whole hour. They were similar in appearance to auroras, yet they possessed some notably different features. (A)______________________________, the group decided to name the phenomenon “Steve,” based on a scene from an animated movie in which some characters give that name to an unfamiliar object.

body:
One evening in late November 1932, a bitterly
cold wind blows fiercely as two figures emerge
from a laboratory. (A) Darkness begins to fall as
they set out into a world of failed banks, collapsed
industry, and widespread despair — a world ruined
by three years of the Great Depression. (B) The
workday has come to an end, but for Pearl
Kendrick and Grace Eldering, a different kind of
work is about to begin. (C) They are on their way
to visit the homes of children suffering from a
deadly disease called pertussis*. (D) Today, infants
usually receive the pertussis vaccine combined with
tetanus and diphtheria toxoids as part of their
routine immunization schedule. The two women go
from home to home collecting samples from the
sick children by the faint light of their lamps.
(E) They listen to the tragic stories of desperate and
unemployed parents as the children, coughing
uncontrollably and struggling to breathe, barely
hold on to life.

lively and exciting
idyllic and peaceful
somber and solemn
romantic and festive

body:
Pertussis is a bacterial disease characterized by serious coughing, breathing difficulties, and the high-pitched “whooping” sound that people with the disease make as they try to breathe in. Because of this distinct sound, people started to call the disease “whooping cough.” For a long time, this terrible illness was one of the greatest terrors of (A)__________________________________, because babies who contracted it had a high chance of dying. In the 1930s, an average of 6,000 people died of whooping cough in the United States each year. Ninety-five percent of them were children under five years of age. The cause of the disease had been identified in 1906, but the vaccines that had been developed were ineffective. Scientists and researchers worked for more than 20 years to produce an effective one, but their efforts were fruitless — until Kendrick and Eldering came along.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: bacteriologists in the US
families with young children
low-income families in the 1930s
elderly people with chronic illnesses
public health officials in the government
solution:
1. 빈칸 뒤에서 백일해에 걸린 아기들은 죽을 확률이 높았다(babies who contracted it had a high chance of dying)고 이유를 밝혔다.
2. 또 1930년대 미국 사망자의 95%가 5세 미만 어린이였다고 했으므로, 이 병은 ‘어린 자녀가 있는 가정’에 가장 큰 공포 중 하나였다.
3. 세균학자(①)·1930년대 저소득 가정(③)·만성 질환 노인(④)·공중보건 공무원(⑤)은 글의 근거와 맞지 않는다.
4. 따라서 답은 ②이다.

They began the process of developing their vaccine by gathering samples of the bacteria that cause whooping cough. To support them, local doctors and nurses provided “cough plates” from their patients. The patients coughed onto a petri dish*, which was then put into an incubator. This allowed the bacteria to grow into colonies that Kendrick and Eldering could analyze. When they collected samples on their own, they would go to the homes of sick children. Each time, they were reminded once again of the dreadful suffering caused by the disease. The sight of these innocent young victims coughing and struggling to breathe was a powerful reminder of the urgent need for an effective vaccine.

When Kendrick and Eldering visited the children’s homes, they found that the symptoms of the disease were less severe than they remembered.
Observing innocent children gasping for air reinforced Kendrick and Eldering’s determination to quickly create a vaccine for whooping cough.

One evening in late November 1932, a bitterly
cold wind blows fiercely as two figures emerge
from a laboratory. Darkness begins to fall as they
set out into a world of failed banks, collapsed
industry, and widespread despair — a world ruined
by three years of the Great Depression. The
workday has come to an end, but for Pearl
Kendrick and Grace Eldering, _________________________

visit the homes of children suffering from a deadly
disease called pertussis*. The two women go from
home to home collecting samples from the sick
children by the faint light of their lamps. They listen
to the tragic stories of desperate and unemployed
parents as the children, coughing uncontrollably and
struggling to breathe, barely hold on to life.

They began the process of developing their
vaccine by gathering samples of the bacteria that
cause whooping cough. To support them, local
doctors and nurses provided “cough plates” from
their patients. The patients coughed onto a petri
dish*, which was then put into an incubator. This
allowed the bacteria to grow into colonies ⓐwhere
Kendrick and Eldering could analyze. When they
collected samples on their own, they would go to
the homes of sick children. Each time, they were
reminded once again of the dreadful suffering
ⓑcaused by the disease. The sight of these
innocent young victims ⓒcoughed and struggled to
breathe was a powerful reminder of the urgent
need for an effective vaccine.

was safe. From 1934 to 1935, they conducted their
first field test with 1,592 children. In the group of
712 vaccinated children, only four developed whooping
cough, and none of these cases were serious.

One evening in late November 1932, a bitterly
cold wind blows fiercely as two figures emerge
from a laboratory. Darkness begins to fall as they
set out into a world of failed banks, collapsed
industry, and widespread despair — a world ruined
by three years of the Great Depression. The
workday has come to an end, but for Pearl
Kendrick and Grace Eldering, a different kind of
work is about to begin. They are on their way to
visit the homes of children suffering from a deadly
disease called pertussis*. The two women go from
home to home collecting samples from the sick
children by the faint light of their lamps. They listen
to the tragic stories of desperate and unemployed
parents as the children, coughing uncontrollably and
struggling to breathe, barely hold on to life.

(B) 앞서 백일해에 대한 개인적 경험이 두 사람 모두에게 연구 에 대한 동기가 되었다고 했으며, 뒤에서는 두 과학자가 아이들 의 건강을 증진시키기를 간절히 바랐다고 했으므로, 자신들이 몸소 겪은 그 질병(백일해)의 극심한 고통을 기억하고 있었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 remembered(기억했다)가 알맞다. Pearl Kendrick studied bacteriology in university and
ⓐwas recruited by the Michigan Department of
Health in 1920. It was there ⓑthat she met fellow
bacteriologist Grace Eldering. The two quickly bonded,
and in 1932 they started working (A)[together /
separately] on a vaccine for whooping cough.
Personal experience served as motivation for both of
them, as they had each survived whooping cough as
children ⓒitself and (B)[forgot / remembered] the
severe pain of the disease. Both scientists were also
eager to promote children’s health.
Unfortunately,
research
funding
was
extremely
limited due to the Great Depression. Also, Kendrick
and Eldering had to develop the vaccine as a
(C)[main / side] project. It was like having a second
job for ⓓwhich they never received any payment.
Still, when they finished their normal duties each
day, they would get started on the work that they
were enthusiastic about. The difficulties they faced
did not stop them from persisting toward their
goal. They did not do the work to make extra
money; instead, they worked ⓔto relieve the
suffering of innocent children and their families.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

Kendrick and Eldering spent many long nights
studying the bacteria
and finally produced a
potential vaccine. Before they performed any clinical
trials, though, they had to be certain that it would
not have any negative side effects on the subjects.
They ran many laboratory tests, and they even
injected it into themselves to confirm that it was
safe. From 1934 to 1935, they conducted their first
field test with 1,592 children. In the group of 712
vaccinated children, only four developed whooping
cough, and none of these cases were serious.

the rigorous testing and successful field trial ofthe new whooping cough vaccine
the difficulties in recruiting a large number ofsubjects for the vaccine field trial
Kendrick and Eldering’s relentless efforts todevelop the vaccine for whooping cough
the ethical controversies surrounding Kendrickand Eldering’s self-injection of the vaccine

Despite the apparent success of the vaccine,
Kendrick and Eldering wanted further confirmation
of its effectiveness. They became determined to
expand their research and run more tests with
larger groups of children. However, they were
unable to proceed because they were facing a
severe lack of funds. With thousands of children
continuing to suffer from the disease, they found
themselves in a desperate situation.
Luckily, they got help from an unexpected figure.
In 1936, First Lady Eleanor Roosevelt herself visited
the laboratory and saw with her own eyes ⓐthe
efforts that Kendrick and Eldering were making in
their
battle
against
whooping
cough.
Eleanor
Roosevelt, whose husband suffered from polio*, was
interested in fighting infectious diseases. She spent
time with the women and came to realize the
enormous importance of their work. With her help,
Kendrick and Eldering were able to secure enough
funding to conduct a large-scale trial.

recommended
immunizations, and soon after, there was a

M: Please welcome our guest, Serena, the teenage
CEO of a successful company.
G: Thank you. I’m glad to be here!

G: Of course. I am the CEO of a tooth-friendly
candy company.

idea?
G: When I was seven, I went to the bank with my
dad and turned down candy a teller offered me
because my parents taught me it’s bad for my
teeth. But kids love candies! That inspired me to
create tasty and tooth-friendly candy.
M: What led you to go beyond just making sweets
and become a CEO?
G: I wanted to make a larger impact. I launched
the Smiles Campaign, continuously donating
candies to schools to promote dental health. I
know how to make a positive impact on kids’
dental health.
M: Impressive! I wish you success!
G: I appreciate it!

body:
A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a
psychology
professor
at
Cornell
University,
reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t
spend your money on things. We assume that the
happiness we get from buying something will last
as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The
trouble with things is that the happiness they
provide fades quickly. There are three critical
reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. What once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
get used to a new possession, we look for an even
better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to
compare themselves with others. We buy a new car
and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better
one, and there’s always someone with a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we
are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves
than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really
like your material stuff. You can even think that
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On
the other hand, your experiences really are part of
you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

choices: The Role of Social Values in Shaping One‘s Identity
The Psychological Drive Behind the Pursuit ofMaterial Wealth
Experiences Over Possessions: The Key to LastingHappiness
Why People Seek Greater Happiness Through NewLife Experiences
The Pursuit of Happiness: Balancing MaterialWealth and Personal Fulfillment

A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a psychology professor at Cornell University, ⓐreached
a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t spend your
money on things. We assume that the happiness
we get from buying something will (A)last as long
as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The trouble with
things is that the happiness they provide ⓑfading
quickly. There are three critical reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. ⓒThat once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep (B)lowering the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
ⓓget used to a new possession, we look for an
even better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans
ⓔto compare themselves with others. We buy a
new car and are (C)thrilled with it until a friend
buys a better one, and there’s always someone with
a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we are
the (D)accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we ⓕhave been.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves than
our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can really
like your material stuff. You can even think  ⓖthat
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain (E)separate from you.
On the other hand, your experiences really are part
of you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

A long-term study conducted by Thomas Gilovich,
a
psychology
professor
at
Cornell
University,
reached a powerful and clear conclusion: Don’t
spend your money on things. We assume that the
happiness we get from buying something will last
as long as the thing itself. But it’s wrong. The
trouble with things is that ⓐ_________________________.
There are three critical reasons for this.
First, we get used to new possessions. What once
seemed novel and exciting quickly becomes the
norm. Second, we keep raising the bar. New
purchases lead to new expectations. As soon as we
get used to a new possession, we look for an even
better one. Third, possessions stimulate humans to
compare themselves with others. We buy a new car
and are thrilled with it until a friend buys a better
one, and there’s always someone with a better one.
Gilovich and other researchers have found that
experiences deliver longer lasting happiness than
things. That’s because experiences become a part of
our identity. We are not our possessions, but we
are the accumulation of everything we’ve seen, the
things we’ve done, and the places we’ve been to.
“Our experiences are a bigger part of ourselves
than our material goods,” says Gilovich. “You can
really like your material stuff. You can even think that
part of your identity is connected to those things,
but nonetheless they remain separate from you. On
the other hand, your experiences really are part of
you. We are the sum total of our experiences.”

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the happiness they evoke doesn‘t last long
the happiness they engender is reinforced byrepeated exposure
the happiness they provide is deeply rooted intheir practical utility
the happiness they elicit is largely dependent onexternal circumstances
the happiness they create is overshadowed bythe responsibilities of ownership
solution: 코넬 대학교 심리학 교수인 Thomas Gilovich가 수행한 장기 연구는 물건에 돈을 쓰지 말라는 명확한 결론에 도달했다고 했으며, 우리가 새로운 소유물들에 익숙해지고, 계속해서 기준 을 높이며, 다른 사람들과 자신을 비교하게 한다는 이유를 제 시하고 있으므로, 물건들의 문제는 그것이 제공하는 행복이 오 래 가지 않는다는 것이라는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸 에는 ❶ ‘그것들이 불러일으키는 행복은 오래 지속되지 않는 다’가 알맞다.

Kool Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential
in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and ⓒ[use / using] the break to show off their

people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls,
short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people
began to dance in groups in the streets and build
a street dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and

early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the

1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of
life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy
who was born there and had to live and die as a
second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose

started a new tradition of social criticism against
injustice. The Message became one of the most
influential rap singles of all time, and was followed
by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same
time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping
made people move or dance. People heard the
social message while moving to the beat.

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final
sound of a word. Most often, (A)it is consciously
used for a musical effect in the final position of
lines within poems or songs. Let’s look at three
ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.
First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this
is called an end rhyme, which is the most
representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the
following example aloud.
My house is so big you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an
ending sound “op.”
Second, words can rhyme within the same line.
This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a
word in the middle of a line and another word in
the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn
Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For
example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not
exactly rhyme, but (B)they create a pattern of
similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect
rhymes, the consonants are identical while the
vowel sounds are different, or the other way round.
When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken
aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This
helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear,
and evokes emotions. So, if you create a rap,
rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger
and reach your listeners.

다음 글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Then where did the word hip-hop originate from?
Nobody knows the exact origin, but the word
hip-hop is said ⓐ[to be / to have been] first used
at a block party. A young man at the party was
about to join the army. His good friend, the MC of
the party, reminded him in a jokey way ⓑ[that / in
which] his days of freedom were over by moving
across the stage like a military instructor to the
beat,
chanting,
“Hip-hop-hip-hop-hip-hop.”
The
crowd loved it. After that, MCs tried out new lines
at parties like “Hip, hop, hippy to the hippy
hop-bop,” “I said a hip-hop, a hibbit, hibby-dibby,
hip-hip-hop and you don’t stop.” Such lines became
a standard part of rap and were included in the
lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album, Rapper’s
Delight (1979), which ⓒ[was / were] an immediate
success.
ⓐ
ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: to bethatwas
to bein whichwere
to have beenthatwere
to have beenthatwas

Hip-hop music began to be a way to express

body:
Imagine an urban area ⓐthat is fast becoming a
slum after an economic recession. Businesses close
their doors and building owners have left. The area
is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating
even in winter. Only those who can’t afford to move
out remain. Unemployment is high, many gangs
emerge, and gang violence between young people
ⓑbecome an everyday thing. Despair is on every
street corner. One day, however, a gang called the
Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its
free meal and medical care programs, decides to
stop fighting and instead persuade young people
ⓒto unite and create a better community. They
suggest a peace treaty. “This is for peace, men. The
violence took away our brothers. We’re not gangsters
anymore. We’ve got to make this town a better
place to live.” Thanks to these new voices, gang
leaders from all over the area sign the treaty. Never
again will they use violence to solve their disputes.
This is the Bronx in the New York of the early
1970s, ⓓwhich hip-hop music was born as a major
part of a new culture of peace created by African
Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop,
now one of the world’s most dominant music
genres, is a ⓔfascinating one. Let’s explore it.

윗글의 첫 번째 문단의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the power of hip-hop in overcoming violenceand despair
the increasing need for community medical careand free meals
the social effects of immigration on Americanurban development
government programs for reducing crime inpoor urban neighborhoods
the desperate situation of a city and a gang’sproposal of a peace treaty to address it
solution: 경기 침체 후 빠르게 슬럼가로 변해가며 젊은이들 사이에 갱 단 폭력이 일상이 된 어느 도시 지역에서 한 갱단이 싸움을 멈추고 젊은이들이 단결해 더 나은 공동체를 만들자고 설득하 기로 결정하여 평화 협정을 제안하고, 이에 지역 전역의 갱단 대표들이 모여 협정에 서명한다는 내용이므로, 글의 주제로 ❺ ‘한 도시의 암울한 상황과 그것을 해결하기 위한 한 갱단의 평 화 협정 제안’이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

body:
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. Abandoned
buildings and parking lots were used for events
called block parties. What eventually emerged from
these parties? A ⓐvibrant youth movement called
hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing,
MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with
music, dance, art, and style.
(A)가장 인기 있는 블록 파티들은 디제이 Kool Herc
에 의해 주최된 것들이었고, 그는 힙합의 창시자로 간
주된다. Herc’s party for his sister’s birthday in
August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of
hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At
this party, using two turntables at the same time,
Herc played two copies of the same record and
then switched between them to ⓑreduce the drum
section known as the break. No longer did people
have to stop dancing at the end of the record
while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool Herc’s style
of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of
hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and use the break to show off their individual
dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing
to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, ⓒshort for
Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to
dance in groups in the streets and build a street
dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over ⓓinstrumental parts of songs to excite
the crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the
beat” and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning
of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both
DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they
asked a friend to take the role of (B)________________
________________________, that is, of the Master of
Ceremonies or MC, at their parties. This ⓔseparate
role became MCing.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: changing records
teaching how to rap
organizing block parties
addressing the audience
coordinating dancers’ movements
solution: Kool Herc와 같은 디제이들이 관중의 흥을 돋우기 위해 박자 와 라임을 넣은 말을 했다는 설명 뒤에 그들이 디제잉과 리듬 감 있는 외침을 동시에 할 수가 없었을 때의 상황이 제시되었 고, 빈칸 뒤에서는 that is(즉)로 사회자 곧 엠씨가 언급되므로, 친구에게 자신을 대신해 관중에게 말을 하는 진행자의 역할을 부탁했다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ❹ ‘청중에 게 말하는 것’이 알맞다. YBM(박준언) 1과

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final
sound of a word. Most often, it is (A)[consciously /
unintentionally] used for a musical effect in the final
position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look
at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.
First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this
is called an end rhyme, which is the most
representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the
following example aloud.
My house is so big you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an
ending sound “op.”
Second, words can rhyme within the same line.
This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a
word in the middle of a line and another word in
the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn
Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For
example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not
exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of
(B)[similar / dissimilar] sounds /s/ and /t/. In most
imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while
the vowel sounds are different, or ⓐthe other way
round.
When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken
aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This
helps the song keep a steady beat, (C)[offends /
pleases] the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you
create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your
voice stronger and reach your listeners.

(B) ‘start’, ‘sport’, ‘straight’는 비슷한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만드는 단어들의 예시이므로, 이 세 단어들이 정확히 라임을 이루진 않지만 유사한 /s/ 소리 및 /t/ 소리의 패턴을 만든다는 흐름이 되는 similar(유사한)가 알맞다. body:
Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of
early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good
time together and boasting about the ability of the
DJ or the rapper. ⓐ______________, a significant shift
occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the
1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The
Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and
Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This
song’s powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of
life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy
who was born there and had to live and die as a
second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose
original aim was creating peace through partying,
started a new tradition of social criticism against
injustice. The Message became one of the most
influential rap singles of all time, and was followed
by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial
discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same
time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping
made people move or dance. People heard the
social message while moving to the beat.
Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop
lyrics, which can be summarized as “respect.”
Hip-hop music began to be a way to express
respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop
pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who
overcame hardship and injustice and went on to
create new music and culture. ⓑ_____________, many
hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much
respect for these heroes. The phrase “something
from nothing,” often used to summarize the genre’s
history, is also an expression of admiration for early
hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the
ghetto despite very limited resources. Rappers also
proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and
perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in
a similar way to the pioneers. This is why the
message of respect is about both self-worth and
respect for others. ⓒ힙합에서 존경이라는 개념의 중
요성은 아무리 강하게 강조해도 지나치지 않다.

ⓐ                    ⓑ
choices: HoweverFurthermore
HoweverHence
SimilarlyMeanwhile
ConsequentlyBesides
As a resultTherefore
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a
slum after an economic recession. Businesses close
their doors and building owners have left. The area
is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating
even in winter. Only those who can’t afford to
move out remain.

men. The violence took away our brothers.
We’re not gangsters anymore. We’ve got to
make this town a better place to live.”

Brothers, which is respected because of its free
meal and medical care programs, decides to
stop fighting and instead persuade young
people to unite and create a better community.
(C) Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and
gang violence between young people becomes an
everyday thing. Despair is on every street corner.

over the area sign the treaty. ⓐ그들은 결코 다시는 그

body:
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought
one another started partying together. ⓐAbandoning
buildings and parking lots were used for events
called block parties. What eventually emerged from
these parties? A vibrant youth movement called
hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing,
MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with
music, dance, art, and style.
The most popular block parties were those hosted
by DJ Kool Herc, ⓑthat is regarded as the founding
father of hip-hop. Herc’s party for his sister’s
birthday in August 1973 is now known as the
birthplace of hip-hop music because of his new DJ
technique. At this party, ⓒusing two turntables at
the same time, Herc played two copies of the same
record and then switched between them to extend
the drum section known as the break. No longer
did people have to stop dancing at the end of the
record while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool
Herc’s style of DJing quickly became influential in
the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing.
The break section became the most anticipated
part of a song. People would form dancer circles
and use the break to show off their individual
dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing
to
his
music
B-Boys
and
B-Girls,
short
for
Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to
dance in groups in the streets and ⓓbuild a street
dance battle culture.
DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and
rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite
the crowd. They would shout phrases like “To the
beat” and “You don’t stop!” This was the beginning
of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn’t do both
DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they
asked a friend ⓔtaking the role of addressing the
audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or
MC, at their parties. This separate role became
MCing.

the gradual decline in the popularity of MCingwithin the B-Boy and B-Girl community
the birth of hip-hop culture and its developmentinfluenced by Kool Herc’s innovative DJ techniques

solution: ㉠ enough가 부사로 쓰여 형용사나 부사를 수식할 때 형용사/ 부사의 뒤에서 수식하므로, 부사 strongly 뒤에 enough가 위치 한 어순의 strongly enough가 알맞다. ㉡ 주어인 명사구 “The HipHop Declaration of Peace”와 두 개의 콤마(,)로 삽입된 부연 설명의 분사구 ‘presented to the UN on May 16th, 2001’에 이어지며, 뒤에 다른 동사(구) 없이 ‘recognize ~ as …(~을 …로 인정하다)’ 표현을 이루는 목적어 hip-hop과 전치사 as, 명사구 ‘an ~ peace’가 있으므로 문장의 동사 자리이다. 따라서 능동태 과거동사 recognized가 알맞다. ㉢ 완전한 절(This ~ Bronx)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지 므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절의 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 This document가 ‘암시하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구(global respect for hip-hop history)가 이어지므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 implying이 알맞다. ㉣ to 뒤의 동사원형 express, fight, bring과 ‘A, B, C, and D’ 의 구조로 병렬 연결되어 명사구 a powerful means를 수식하 는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사구를 이루어야 하므로, 동사원형 be가 알맞다.

body:
A rhyme is usually the repetition of the final sound of a word. Most often, it is consciously used for a musical effect in the final position of lines within poems or songs. Let’s look at three ways that rhyme is used in rap lyrics.

First, if two lines finish with words that rhyme, this is called an end rhyme, which is the most representative kind of rhyme. Try reading the following example aloud.
My house is so big that you cannot see the top
Don’t jump off the roof that is quite a long drop
The two rhyming words “top” and “drop” share an ending sound “op.”

Second, words can rhyme within the same line. This creates an internal rhyme, which involves a word in the middle of a line and another word in the same or the next line. For example,
They’re never gonna learn how to wait their turn

Third, rappers often use imperfect rhymes. For example, “start,” “sport,” and “straight” do not exactly rhyme, but they create a pattern of similar sounds /s/ and /t/. In most imperfect rhymes, the consonants are identical while the vowel sounds are different, or the other way round.

When a sequence of rhymed words is spoken aloud, it creates a rhythmic pattern or “flow.” This helps the song keep a steady beat, pleases the ear, and evokes emotions. So, if you create a rap, rhyming is a great way to make your voice stronger and reach your listeners.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Why Rhyming Matters in Rap Lyrics
Perfect Rhymes: The Key to Successful Rap
How Rappers Come Up with Great Rhymes
The Types and Effects of Rhymes in Rap Lyrics
The Emotional Power of Rhyming in Rap Lyrics

Our final destination was Uluru, the largest rock in
the world. I’ve longed to see it in person ever since
I came across a picture of it a few years ago.
When I finally laid eyes on Uluru after an
exhausting train ride, I couldn’t believe ⓐthat I was
seeing. Could this gigantic mountain really be a
single piece of rock? From a distance, it looked like
a huge red dome, ⓑwas providing an amazing
contrast against the clear blue sky.
 The next day, we walked around its 10-kilometer
base. Along the way, we saw numerous caves,
ⓒsome of them displayed a distinct gray hue. My
uncle informed me that Uluru was naturally gray,
but that its iron content had oxidized over time,
giving it its iconic red color.
 The highlight of our visit was the sunset. Prior to
my trip, I had learned that the color of the sunsets
at Uluru ⓓchange over time based on the sun’s
position and the intensity of sunlight. When I finally
saw one, the colors transformed from red to deep
orange and then to purple as the sun sank below
the horizon. It was impossible ⓔto be found words
to describe the beauty I was seeing. It was the
most memorable night of my entire journey.

body:
Kakadu National Park is the largest national park
in northern Australia. Although the trip was long
and tiring, the park’s natural beauty immediately
revitalized us. The landscape resembled an ocean
filled with green eucalyptus trees, and the air was
incredibly refreshing! Perhaps the only drawback
was that being in a remote region, we had no
Wi-Fi connection. (A)_____________, we quickly adapted
and embraced the quiet and peaceful vacation
atmosphere.
 One of the highlights of our visit there was our
tour led by Victor, an Aboriginal guide. He
explained that Kakadu has been home to Aboriginal
people for over 40,000 years. He also introduced us
to rock art sites depicting Aboriginal stories. ⓐ내가
특히 흥미롭게 느낀 한 그림은 엑스레이 스타일로 그
려진 것으로, 어떤 부분들을 먹을 수 있는지 보여 주
기 위해 물고기의 내부를 묘사한 것이었다. Other
fascinating drawings showed things like a spirit
creating lightning and a hunter holding a spear.
 (B)_____________, Kakadu is famous for its saltwater
crocodiles, as there are around 10,000 living in the
region. They are the largest of all crocodile species
and grow up to six meters long! While crossing the
Yellow River, we spotted over 30 of them! Being
able to see them right in front of me was an
experience that I will never forget.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
choices: HoweverIn fact
As a resultTherefore
For exampleConversely
For instanceIn addition
NeverthelessFurthermore
solution: (A) Kakadu 국립 공원은 외딴 지역이라 Wi-Fi가 없었다는 단점 을 언급한 후, 우리는 그것에 빠르게 적응하고 평화로운 분위 기를 받아들였다는 긍정의 흐름이 이어지므로, However(하지 만) 또는 Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고)가 알맞다. (B) Kakadu 국립 공원에서 원주민 이야기를 묘사한 암각화 유적 지를 가이드에게서 소개받았다는 설명에 이어, Kakadu의 볼거리 로 약 10,000마리의 바다악어로도 유명하다는 설명이 이어지므 로, ‘게다가’라는 뜻의 In addition 또는 Furthermore가 알맞다.

system. There are several regions you can visit to
see it, and I chose to explore Lady Elliot Island in
the southern region, which is known for its
beautiful coral reefs and manta rays.

see. The water was different shades of blue and
green, depending on the depth of the sea and
the coral formations underneath. Endless patches
of white sand added to the breathtaking
scenery. It was so beautiful, and I couldn’t wait
to dive into the crystal-clear water!
(C) As I wanted to explore the coral reef more
closely, I went snorkeling. The first sight that
greeted me in the water was manta rays. Even
though they are endangered, I witnessed many

also encountered sea turtles and a school of

Our final destination was Uluru, the largest rock in
the world. I’ve longed to see it ⓐin person ever
since I came across a picture of it a few years ago.
When I finally laid eyes on Uluru after an
exhausting train ride, I couldn’t believe what I was
seeing. Could this ⓑmodest mountain really be a
single piece of rock? From a distance, it looked like
a huge red dome, providing an amazing ⓒcontrast
against the clear blue sky.
 The next day, we walked around its 10-kilometer
base. Along the way, we saw numerous caves, some
of which displayed a distinct gray hue. My uncle
informed me that Uluru was naturally gray, but that
its iron content had ⓓoxidized over time, giving it
its iconic red color.
 The highlight of our visit was the sunset. Prior to
my trip, I had learned that the color of the sunsets
at Uluru changes over time based on the sun’s
position and the intensity of sunlight. When I finally
saw one, the colors transformed from red to deep
orange and then to purple as the sun sank below
the horizon. It was impossible to find words to
describe the beauty I was seeing. It was the most
ⓔmemorable night of my entire journey.

system. There are several regions you can visit to
see it, and I chose to explore Lady Elliot Island in
the southern region, which is known for its
beautiful coral reefs and manta rays.
As our plane approached land, I spotted the Great
Barrier Reef, ⓐstretching as far as I could see. The
water was different shades of blue and green,
depending on the depth of the sea and the coral
formations underneath. Endless patches of white
sand added to the breathtaking scenery. It was so
beautiful, and I couldn’t wait to dive into the
crystal-clear water!
 As I wanted to explore the coral reef more closely,
I went snorkeling. The first sight that greeted me in
the water ⓑwas manta rays. Even though they are
endangered, I witnessed many mantas ⓒgliding
elegantly through the water. I also encountered sea
turtles and a school of tropical fish. It was the coral
reef, however, ⓓthat impressed me the most that
day. It was a spectacular burst of colors and life!
My uncle later informed me ⓔthat many parts of
the Great Barrier Reef, especially in the northern
region, suffer from coral bleaching, which turns the
reef white. I felt bad when I heard that and hoped
the reef would recover soon.

Hello, everyone. Today we’ll discuss how to
effectively set goals using SMART strategies. SMART
stands for “specific, measurable, achievable, relevant,
and
time-bound.”
When
setting
a
goal,
it’s
important to be specific about what you want to
achieve. And make your goal measurable so you
can check your progress. Your goal should also be
realistically possible to achieve and relevant to your
life. Lastly, set a time limit to achieve it. For
example, if you used to say, “I want better grades,”
now say, “I aim to raise my math grade from a B
to an A by the end of the semester.” Use these
SMART strategies to set goals from now on. Thank
you.

body:
Hello, everyone. Today we’ll discuss how to
effectively set goals using SMART strategies. SMART
stands for “specific, measurable, achievable, relevant,
and
time-bound.”
When
setting
a
goal,
it’s
important to be specific about what you want to
achieve. And make your goal measurable so you
can check your progress. Your goal should also be
realistically possible to achieve and relevant to your
life. Lastly, set a time limit to achieve it. For
example, if you used to say, “I want better grades,”
now say, “I aim to raise my math grade from a B
to an A by the end of the semester.” Use these
SMART strategies to set goals from now on. Thank
you.

위 담화의 SMART에 대한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Keep your goal broad rather than clearly definingwhat you want to achieve.
Frame your goal in a way that lets you trackhow far you have come.
Choose a goal that you can realistically reach.
Make sure your goal ties into your own life.
Give yourself a deadline for reaching your goal.
solution: 화자는 목표를 세울 때 무엇을 이루고 싶은지 구체적으로 정해야 한다고 말한다. 그런데 ❶ '이루고 싶은 것을 명확히 정하기보다 목 표를 포괄적으로 설정하라.'는 구체적인 목표를 강조하는 담화 내 용과 반대되므로 일치하지 않는다.

body:
[What to Change]
Give Yourself a New Identity
ⓐ당신은 며칠 이상 좋은 습관을 기르고 유지하는 것
이 어렵다고 생각할 수도 있다. This often happens
when people focus on changing external outcomes
or behaviors rather than on where they originate
from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you achieve. The
middle layer is process — what you do. The deepest
and most fundamental layer is identity — what you
believe or who you are. While changes in all three
layers are useful in their own way, the key to lasting
success lies in the direction of change. True
behavior change occurs when there is a shift in your
identity from within. If your new habit is not in
harmony with your identity, it is unlikely to last.
You can work on changing your identity through
two steps. First, keep asking yourself, “What kind of
person do I want to become?” Once you have an
idea of the kind of person you want to be, start
reinforcing
that
identity
through
your
actions.
Specifically, repeat the action that kind of person
would choose to do, and over time, you will
naturally become such a person. For example, if you
want to start exercising daily, think of yourself as
an energetic and motivated person who cares about
his or her health. Then try to do the routines that
such a person would naturally do. Repeating these
routines will gradually lead you to become that
kind of person.

When ⓐcreating a new habit, set a cue that
sparks the habit and ⓑmakes the cue as obvious
as possible. (A) The two most common cues are
time and location. (B) The formula for your action
plan can be “I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in
[LOCATION].” Instead of a vague intent like “I will
work out,” be specific and tell ⓒyou “I will work
out for an hour starting at 8 p.m. at home.”
(C) Your current habit is already associated with a
particular time and location, so ⓓpairing it with a new
one by saying something like “After I [CURRENT
HABIT], I will [NEW HABIT].” (D) Your action plan can
be “After I finish dinner around 8 p.m., I’ll immediately
change into my workout clothes.” (E) The more this
link between the cue and the action is repeated, ⓔthe
more firmly the new habit will be rooted in your life.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ makes → make (등위접속사 and에 의해 앞의 명령문 동사 set과 병렬을 이루므로 동사원형 make로 고친다. that sparks the habit은 선행사 a cue를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사절이다. makes를 쓰면 관계사절의 동사 sparks와 병렬을 이루어 a cue 가 makes의 주어가 된다. 이때 목적어 the cue가 문맥상 주어 a cue와 동일한 대상을 가리키므로 재귀대명사 itself를 써야 하며, ‘단서가 자기 자신을 분명하게 만든다’라는 의미가 되어 본문의 의도와도 어긋난다.) ⓒ you → yourself (명령문의 생략된 주어는 you이며, tell의 목적어 가 주어와 같은 대상을 가리키므로 재귀대명사 yourself로 고친다.) ⓓ pairing → pair (등위접속사 so 뒤에서 새로운 습관과 현재 습관을 연결하라고 권하는 명령문이 이어져야 하므로, 동명사 pairing을 동사원형 pair로 고친다.)

body:
W: We often hear that self-care is important, but
what is it exactly and how can we do it?
[What is self-care?]
Lisa: I think self-care is loving yourself and making
sure that you’re okay physically and mentally.
Jake: I see self-care as a battery recharge.
Nari: Self-care is looking after yourself and checking
whether you can continue doing your daily
routine.
[Why is self-care important?]
Lisa: Self-care is important because it prevents
burnout and helps you manage your stress.
Jake: Through self-care, you can restore your energy
so that you can fully enjoy your life.
Nari: Self-care helps you improve and make better
decisions.
[What can you do in terms of self-care?]
Lisa: There are many different things you can do,
so it’s important to figure out what works for
you. As for me, I treat myself to delicious
food.
Jake: Being social is a big thing for me. When I
hang out with my family or friends, I feel
re-energized.
Nari: I like to watch cat videos. It gives me a sense
of healing. I strongly recommend it.

위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: For Lisa, self-care means loving herself andlooking after her body and mind.
Jake compares the effects of self-care tocharging up a drained battery.
Nari defines self-care as checking whether shecan keep up her daily routine.
Nari believes that watching cat videos helps hermake wiser everyday decisions.
Lisa treats herself to good food as a way oftaking care of herself.
solution: 나리는 셀프케어가 더 나은 판단을 내리는 데 도움이 된다고 말했지만, 이는 셀프케어 전반의 효용으로 언급한 것일 뿐 고 양이 영상 시청과 직접 연결 지어 말한 것은 아니다. 고양이 영상에 대해서는 치유되는 느낌을 준다고만 언급했으므로, ❹ '고양이 영상을 보는 것이 더 현명한 일상적 결정을 내리는 데 도움을 준다고 생각한다'는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

What is rewarded is repeated. When a behavior feels rewarding and satisfying, people are likely to repeat it. To maintain a new habit, it is important to experience a sense of immediate accomplishment, even in small ways. In fact, simply knowing that you are making progress is a quick and powerful motivating reward in itself. One effective method of keeping track of your progress is to use a habit tracker. This tool lets you use a formula like “After I [NEW HABIT], I will [TRACK MY HABIT].” For example, you can write “After I finish my daily workout, I’ll record it in my workout journal.” This provides you with moments of satisfaction, which helps you stick to your new habit.

[How to Change]
Make Your Habit an Automatic Loop
After defining your desired identity, you will want
to integrate new habits into your daily routines. It
is worth noting here (A)[what / that] any lasting
habits ⓐ______________________________. To make habits
take effect almost automatically, we need to
understand the concept of the habit loop, which
consists of four steps: cue, craving, response, and
reward. The more smoothly this loop operates, the
more easily the habit is performed. The following
four laws offer practical guidance for each step.
The 1st Law: Cue
“Make an obvious cue for your habit.”
When creating a new habit, set a cue that sparks
the habit and make the cue as (B)[obvious /
obviously] as possible. The two most common cues
are time and location. The formula for your action
plan can be “I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in
[LOCATION].” Instead of a vague intent like “I will
work out,” (C)[being / be] specific and tell yourself “I
will work out for an hour starting at 8 p.m. at home.”
Another effective method is habit stacking. Your
current habit is already associated with a particular
time and location, so pair it with a new one by
saying something like “After I [CURRENT HABIT], I
will [NEW HABIT].” Your action plan can be “After I
finish dinner around 8 p.m., I’ll immediately change
into my workout clothes.” The more this link
between the cue and the action is repeated, the
more firmly the new habit will be rooted in your life.

윗글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: whatobviousbeing
whatobviouslybeing
thatobviousbeing
thatobviouslybe
thatobviousbe
solution: (A) 뒤에 주어 any lasting habits와 동사 take를 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. what은 선행 사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 뒤에 불완전한 절이 이어져야 한다. (B) ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’의 구조에서 목적어 the cue의 상태 를 설명하는 목적격보어가 필요하므로 형용사 obvious가 적절하다. (C) 전치사구 Instead of a vague intent like “I will work out” 뒤에 행동을 권하는 명령문이 이어지며, be와 tell이 등위접속 사 and에 의해 병렬 연결되므로 동사원형 be가 적절하다.

body:
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you (A)[want /
achieve]. The middle layer is process — what you
(B)[avoid / do]. The deepest and most fundamental
layer is identity — what you believe or who you are.
While changes in all three layers are useful in their
own way, the key to lasting success lies in the
direction of change. True behavior change occurs
when there is a shift in your identity from within. If
your new habit is not in harmony with your identity,
it is (C)[likely / unlikely] to last.

When you enjoy doing something, a chemical
substance (A)[called / calling] dopamine is released in
your brain, which increases your motivation and makes
you eager to repeat the action. Thus, it is crucial to
make your habits attractive and enjoyable. This is
(B)[where / what] a strategy known as temptation
bundling comes into play. Temptation bundling works
by linking [ACTION I WANT] with [HABIT I NEED]. For
example, if you want to watch your favorite TV show
but need to work out, you can bundle these two
actions together by watching the show only while
exercising on your stationary bike in the living room.
This way, you can seamlessly do what you need to do
along with (C)[what / which] you want to do.

prefer actions that require less effort. If a habit is

important to create an environment that makes
habits easier to do.

you could set up a dedicated workout area like

becomes significantly easier to continue.

is readily available while keeping distractions
away. Another approach is the two-minute rule.

Playing sports is one of the most common hobbies, but people also love to watch live sports games. If you go to any sports stadium, you will be able to find fans cheering wildly, crying with joy. In the case of football, some famous matches are accompanied by (A)[extreme / moderate] fans, whose overly aggressive support of their team sometimes leads to confrontations with fans from opposition teams. If someone’s joy, sadness, and even anger emerge from the love of their team, what makes them so (B)[devoted / apathetic]? What does it mean for an individual to be a sports fan? And would their passion and cheering actually influence the performance of their team? These questions can be addressed from both an evolutionary and a social psychological perspective.

From an evolutionary perspective, sports fandom emerged from our tribal hunter-gatherer ancestors tens of thousands of years ago. At that time, a person was far more likely to (C)[fail / survive] as a member of a group than as an isolated individual. People could help each other in groups when dealing with difficult tasks, such as carrying hunted animals that were too heavy for one person to handle. This mutual cooperation built trust and fostered relationships among group members. In fact, group membership was so important that tribes with a stronger sense of community were more likely to defeat tribes whose members were less closely allied. Because of this, community membership was a survival mechanism for our ancestors, and the instinct to find one’s own tribe or group has been passed down to modern people. This may be how community membership influences our choice of a sports team and our sense of loyalty to that team.

body:
In the past, being a fan of a Korean pop idol typically meant waving colored balloons at concerts and sending gifts. Most fans, often teenagers, admired their idols from a distance. However, over the past three decades, the K-pop fandom culture has evolved dramatically with the development of digital technology. Today, fans actively engage themselves in communication with their idols through social media platforms. They can provide feedback and suggestions, which can have a beneficial influence on their idols. When they see some positive changes in their idols, they feel rewarded for their contribution. In other words, fans have changed from consumers to active participants in the K-pop phenomenon. In addition to this change in their attitudes and roles, today’s fans express their affection in different ways. Instead of showering their idols with material gifts, they organize fundraising and volunteer activities in the name of their idols. For example, fans of a popular idol group have raised funds to support children’s charities. Fans’ efforts not only promote good images of their idols but also foster the value of sharing. This change in fandom culture shows how fans’ interaction with K-pop idols has become more dynamic and meaningful. The new culture brings fans closer to their idols and provides a more inclusive and rewarding experience for them.

Evolving from ㉠__________ spectators to co-creators of the K-pop phenomenon, modern fans ㉡__________ their influence on idols through digital media and various meaningful ㉢__________ activities.
choices: ㉠ receptive — ㉡ exert — ㉢ commercial
㉠ receptive — ㉡ exert — ㉢ social
㉠ receptive — ㉡ eliminate — ㉢ social
㉠ assertive — ㉡ exert — ㉢ commercial
㉠ assertive — ㉡ eliminate — ㉢ social
solution:
1. ㉠ 과거 팬들은 멀리서 우상을 동경만 하는(admired their idols from a distance) ‘수동적인(receptive)’ 관객이었다.
2. ㉡ 오늘날 팬들은 SNS로 우상과 소통하며 피드백을 주어 우상에게 긍정적 영향을 ‘미친다(exert)’. eliminate(없애다)는 반대이다.
3. ㉢ 물질적 선물 대신 모금·봉사 활동을 조직하므로 ‘사회적(social)’ 활동이다. commercial(상업적)은 글과 맞지 않는다.
4. 따라서 답은 ②이다.

inclusion by supporting the same team with other

body:
(A)우리가 스포츠팀을 응원하는 이유를 설명해 줄 수
있는 두 가지 사회심리학적 이론들 또한 있다:
optimal distinctiveness and basking in reflected
glory. Though it may be human nature to form a
group and feel a sense of belonging to that group,
being a fan of a sports team is different from just
having friends. Optimal distinctiveness theory states
that everyone has a need for inclusion and
differentiation. That is, individuals want to be
included somewhere, but they also want to be
different
and
unique.
These
two
basic
but
competing needs can be satisfied through group
membership. Sports team supporters are one such
group. For example, if you are a fan of a football
team based in your city, you can satisfy your need
for inclusion by supporting the same team with
other in-group members. This can also make you
feel unique because your team’s fans are different
from the fans of other teams. This feeling of
uniqueness is reinforced by sports teams’ deliberate
use of their team colors and songs.

When people think of a changing climate, images of melting glaciers and polar bears ⓐ[losing / lost] their habitat often come to mind. But this is only one aspect of the problem. Climate change is causing extreme weather conditions, ⓑ[that / which] have become more frequent and intense worldwide. Heatwaves, droughts, floods, and wildfires are affecting countries around the world. In the autumn of 2019, for example, Australia was hit by one of the worst wildfires on record. Over six months, the wildfires burned about 10 million hectares of land, and killed hundreds of millions of animals. Approximately 30 percent of the koalas in the region are said to ⓒ[be / have been] killed due to the fires.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: ⓐ losing — ⓑ that — ⓒ be
ⓐ lost — ⓑ that — ⓒ have been
ⓐ losing — ⓑ which — ⓒ be
ⓐ lost — ⓑ which — ⓒ have been
ⓐ losing — ⓑ which — ⓒ have been
solution:
1. ⓐ 북극곰이 서식지를 ‘잃는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어 their habitat가 있으므로 능동의 현재분사 losing이 알맞다.
2. ⓑ 콤마 뒤에서 extreme weather conditions를 부연하는 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 자리이므로 which가 알맞다(that은 계속적 용법으로 쓸 수 없다).
3. ⓒ 코알라가 죽은 것은 ‘말해지는(are said)’ 지금보다 앞선 2019년의 일이므로 완료부정사 to have been (killed)가 알맞다.
4. 따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

in tidal flats located around the ocean. Research
conducted in 2021 has revealed that getbol in
Korea stores approximately 13 million tons of
carbon and absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon
dioxide each year. This means that getbol alone can
offset the carbon dioxide emissions produced by
110,000 cars in a year. Considering that getbol

carbon has become a promising and sustainable
solution to the current environmental problem.

capabilities of tidal flats with the goal of having
them officially recognized as blue carbon.

energy-consuming network, ⓒcontributing to climate

messages in data centers ⓓcreate carbon emissions.
These data centers rely on huge servers to store
and access data at all times. Because the centers
use electricity to run the servers and to cool down
the large amounts of heat ⓔthat they generate,
they consume a significant amount of fossil fuels.
Mike Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author
of How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of
Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For

carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a
long email, which takes about ten minutes to write
and three minutes to read on a computer, has a
footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So, something as
simple as deleting unnecessary email messages can
help to save the Earth.

environment.

there’s always something we can do for it.

travels] between Australia and the Russian Far East
or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover

during their long journeys, and they would become

getbol
is
ⓔnot
only
a
unique

protect personal information online

Blue Carbon and Getbol
One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon
in the atmosphere is to (A)____________________________
________________________. The Earth’s carbon can be
divided into three types: black carbon, green
carbon, and blue carbon. Black carbon is released
while burning fossil fuels, such as coal, oil, and gas.
It causes the greenhouse effect, leading to global
warming and climate change. Green carbon, on the
other hand, is carbon absorbed by and stored in
land
ecosystems,
such
as
rainforests
like
the
Amazon in South America. It plays a vital role in
maintaining the ecosystem because it absorbs
carbon dioxide through photosynthesis. Finally, blue
carbon is the carbon stored in the ocean, including
coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangrove
wetlands, seagrass beds, and tidal marshes. The
carbon absorption rate of marine ecosystems is
about 50 times faster than that of land ecosystems.
Blue carbon can store up to 10 times more carbon
per unit area than forests on land, making it highly
cost-effective.
(B)청색 탄소의 눈에 띄는 예는 대양 주변에 위치한
갯벌에서 발견될 수 있다. Research conducted in
2021 has revealed that getbol in Korea stores
approximately 13 million tons of carbon and
absorbs over 260,000 tons of carbon dioxide each
year. This means that getbol alone can offset the
carbon dioxide emissions produced by 110,000 cars
in
a
year.
Considering
that
getbol
contains
numerous organisms and marine animals that store
carbon, the treasure house of blue carbon has
become a promising and sustainable solution to the
current environmental problem. Scientists worldwide
are continuing to explore the capabilities of tidal
flats with the goal of having them officially
recognized as blue carbon.

ban the use of fossil fuels completely
exploit useless rainforests for commercial use
relocate urban industrial facilities to the coastline
accelerate the development of green energytechnologies
solution: 정답은 ① 이다. (해설 없음)

Thanks to its rich biodiversity, getbol is visited by about 118 species of migratory birds every year. For millions of migratory birds that travel between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska, Korea’s tidal flats are a vital stopover location. Without getbol, they would not have a place to rest and feed themselves during their long journeys, and they would become extinct. Since getbol is not only a unique ecosystem crowded with diverse species but also a resting place for endangered birds, it was added to the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021. It includes the four tidal flats on the western and southern coasts of Korea: Seocheon Getbol, Gochang Getbol, Shinan Getbol, and Boseong-Suncheon Getbol.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The remarkable species diversity found in getbol allows roughly 118 kinds of migratory birds to visit the site annually.
Getbol serves as an essential staging site for millions of migratory birds flying between Australia and the Russian Far East or Alaska.
If it were not for getbol, offering rest and food during their long journeys, millions of migratory birds would be in danger of extinction.
As a distinctive habitat for diverse wildlife and threatened bird species, getbol earned a place on the UNESCO World Natural Heritage List in 2021.
All four mudflats designated as UNESCO World Natural Heritage sites are located only along Korea’s western coastline.

solution: ⓑ conducting → conducted (동사구 has revealed에 대한 주 어 Research를 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 쓰일 수 있 으나, 수식받는 명사 Research가 ‘행해진’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어 진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 conducting 을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 conducted로 고친다.) ⓕ caused → causing (완전한 절(This ~ flats) 뒤에 접속사 없이 동 사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로 흐름상 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구 문을 이끄는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 원인에 해당하는 앞 절의 내용 이 ‘초래한’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 a loss of biodiversity가 있으므로, caused를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 causing으로 고친다.) ⓖ Had it not been for → Were it not for[If it were not for] 또는 Without[But for] (주절에 ‘조동사 과거형+동사원형’인 would fail이 쓰였으며 흐름상 과거 사실이 아닌 현재 사실과 반 대되는 일을 가정하고 있으므로, ‘~이 없다면, …할 것이다’를 뜻 하는 가정법 과거 표현인 ‘Were it not for[If it were not for/But for/Without] ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+동사원형 …’을 써야 한다. 따라서 과거 사실의 반대를 가정하는 가정법 과거완료 표현인 ‘Had it not been for[If it had not been for/Without/But for] ~, 주어+조동사 과거형+have+p.p. …(~가 없었다면, …했을 것이다)’ 의 Had it not been for를 Were it not for, If it were not for, But for, Without 중 하나로 고친다.)

One of the most promising ways to reduce carbon
in the atmosphere is to use the “good” carbon on
Earth. The Earth’s carbon can be divided into three
types: black carbon, green carbon, and blue carbon.
Black carbon is released while burning fossil fuels,
such as coal, oil, and gas. It causes the greenhouse
effect, leading to global warming and climate
change. Green carbon, on the other hand, is carbon
absorbed by and stored in land ecosystems, such as
rainforests like the Amazon in South America. It
plays a vital role in maintaining the ecosystem
because
it
absorbs
carbon
dioxide
through
photosynthesis. Finally, blue carbon is the carbon
stored in the ocean, including coastal and marine
ecosystems such as mangrove wetlands, seagrass
beds, and tidal marshes. The carbon absorption rate
of marine ecosystems is about 50 times faster than
that of land ecosystems. Blue carbon can store up
to 10 times more carbon per unit area than forests
on land, making it highly cost-effective.
choices: Replacing fossil fuels with green carbon sourceswill eliminate the risk of global warming.
Black carbon must be converted into blue carbonto increase the overall rate of photosynthesis.
Preserving marine ecosystems can be a highlyefficient strategy for mitigating climate change.
Land ecosystems are more cost-effective thanmarine ecosystems in absorbing carbon dioxide.
Mangrove wetlands and tidal marshes absorbcarbon at a slower rate than rainforests like theAmazon.

body:
This is why the international community has been
ⓐ[seeking / sought] solutions to the climate crisis.
In 2015, 195 countries signed the Paris Agreement
to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C above
pre-industrial levels. The countries agreed upon the
fact ⓑ[that / what] the increase in atmospheric
carbon is a major reason for climate change. One
key strategy to combat it is to achieve “carbon
neutrality,” which ⓒ[involve / involves] maintaining a
balance between the amount of carbon emitted and
carbon absorbed.
The Earth’s Atmosphere Is Like a Bathtub
Let’s imagine that the Earth’s atmosphere is a
large bathtub, and the greenhouse gases emitted
into the atmosphere are like water flowing from a
tap into the bathtub. At the bottom of the bathtub,
there’s a drain that lets the water out. If we keep
the tap running, the water level in the bathtub will
rise, just as greenhouse gas emissions have led to
an increase in atmospheric carbon. This rise in
carbon levels has already resulted in negative
environmental
consequences,
such
as
climate
change. To make matters worse, if the water is not
effectively drained, the bathtub will overflow. In
other words, if we don't reduce carbon emissions
sufficiently, atmospheric carbon will continue to
accumulate.

ⓒ
choices: seekingthatinvolve

solution: ⓐ why가 이끄는 절의 주어 the international community가 기후 위기에 대한 해결책을 ‘찾는’ 주체이며, 뒤에 solutions 이하의 명사구가 목적어로 이어지므로, 능동태인 현재완료 진행형 (have[has]+been+-ing)을 이루는 현재분사 seeking이 알맞다. ⓑ 추상명사구 the fact의 구체적 내용에 해당하는 완전한 절(the increase ~ change)을 연결하므로, 동격 접속사 that이 알맞다. ⓒ 콤마(,) 뒤에 쓰인 주격 관계대명사 which가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이며, 관계사절이 부연 설명하는 선행사 “carbon neutrality”가 단수명사구이므로, 단수동사로 수일치한 involves 가 알맞다.

Email is one of the most widely used forms of
communication today. Did you know that the
seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or
checking your inbox has an environmental impact?
(A) Because the centers use electricity to run the
servers and to cool down the large amounts of
heat that they generate, they consume a significant
amount of fossil fuels. Mike Berners-Lee, the
British researcher and author of How Bad Are
Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of Everything,
looked at our average email traffic.
(B) In reality, email travels through an energy-consuming
network, contributing to climate change on our
planet. Storing countless email messages in data
centers creates carbon emissions. These data
centers rely on huge servers to store and access
data at all times.
(C) For example, a short phone-to-phone email has a
carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But,
a long email, which takes about ten minutes to
write and three minutes to read on a computer,
has a footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So,
something as simple as deleting unnecessary
email messages can help to save the Earth.

A

body:
Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. (A)그는 물리학의 천재로 여겨짐에도 불구하고,
뛰어난 선원이 아니었으며, 자신의 항해술에도 신경
쓰지 않았다. His technique remained at a basic
level, which was simply to “Set sail, make it fast, no
thoughts of energy or speed, lean back, let the
boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place where he could be
completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his
boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the
apparent meaninglessness of his sailing adventures.
Watching the waves while on his boat, Einstein
forgot all his worries. Like Einstein, for many people,
hobbies just provide the conditions for a sense of
pure satisfaction.

Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do in their free time. In the past, though, this probably wasn’t true because most people had to work long hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time must have been hard to come by. However, the Industrial Revolution and the labor movement that followed it led to a gradual decrease in working hours to eight-hour work days and five-day work weeks. For the first time in history, a majority of people had free time to enjoy activities that they found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.

body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person to walk through the trail, which is
known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually start in
early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with a
low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting
a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the PCT.
In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. (A) Hikers cook their
own meals, and sometimes they have to endure
days without eating. (B) Hikers are advised to carry
the latest PCT Water Report, a list of all water
sources. (C) When it comes to sleeping, most hikers
sleep in tents, and in some areas, they can use
shelters to stay safe from the harsh weather. (D) If
you are lucky, you may find “trail angels,” who
provide transportation to close towns, meals, or
other forms of assistance. (E)
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to
see
the
magnificent
landscapes
of
the
American West.

how to address the low completion rate of thefive-month hike
the personal benefits of experiencing a longjourney in nature
the diverse geographical features and climaticvariations across the U.S.

Hobbies Create Community
J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.

histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former inspired
by Welsh, and the latter inspired by Finnish and
Latin. But inventing languages was a frustrating

ashamed of spending the valuable commodity of
time
for
their
private

Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people to learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in (C)[private /
public], they can easily find other like-minded
people to share their passion, celebrate their
achievements, and encourage each other along the
way. They could even work together on language
projects that Tolkien may have never been able to
imagine.

(B)
(C)

solution: (A) 다음 문장에서 톨킨이 자신과 언어를 사랑하는 다른 사람 들이 겪었던 고립감(isolation)에 대해 글을 썼다고 했으므로 ‘isolate(고립시키다)’가 적절하다. (B) 앞에서, 사람들이 부끄러워하며 자신들의 사적인 즐거움을 위해 시간이라는 귀중한 재화를 쓰는 것을 부끄러워한다고 했 으므로 더 높은 수준의 언어적 발전은 결국 비밀스러운 장소 에 갇히게 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘secret(비밀스러 운)’이 적절하다. (C) 과거에는 혼자 작업했던 것과 달리 현재는 인터넷의 발달 로 다른 이들과 소통할 수 있고, 열정을 공유할 마음이 맞는 사람들을 쉽게 찾을 수 있다고 했으므로 ‘개인적으로 자신의 프로젝트를 진행하는 대신에’라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘(in) private(개인적으로)’이 적절하다.

Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long

body:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If you meet someone who has woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer are titles that people are proud to call themselves. On the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t considered serious hobbies because there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.

What effort is required for an activity to qualify as a serious hobby?

What motivates people to choose a particular hobby over other activities?

body:
Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve their
skills, some ⓐdo for the sheer pleasure of doing it.
Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he was 18
years old, ⓑventured out on the lakes in Switzerland
and simply enjoying the time on his boat. He continued
to enjoy sailing as a life-long sailor. Although he is
considered a genius in physics, he wasn’t a good sailor,
nor did he care about his sailing technique. His
technique remained at a basic level, ⓒwhich was simply
to “Set sail, make it fast, no thoughts of energy or
speed, lean back, let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain ⓓwhy he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, ⓔit was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of sailing
to go to a place where he could be completely
relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his boat Tinef,
meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the apparent
meaninglessness of his sailing adventures. Watching
the waves while on his boat, Einstein forgot all his
worries. Like Einstein, for many people, hobbies just
provide the conditions for a sense of pure satisfaction.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Some people do hobbies to build their skills,while others do them just because they enjoythe activities themselves.
Einstein started sailing at a young age andsimply enjoyed being on his boat, even thoughhe was not an expert at it.
Einstein may have named his boat Tinef becausehe regarded his worries and anxieties as worthless.
For Einstein, sailing was a way to find a placewhere he could fully rest.
As Einstein’s case shows, hobbies can providepeople with the right conditions to experiencea feeling of pure satisfaction.

른다. That is, it sometimes leads to an unexpected

Bopp, a manager at a construction materials factory
and an (B)amateur astronomer, discovered the
comet Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his
friends in the Arizona desert. To make the story

is
not
alone.
Numerous
amateur
astronomers have discovered comets, stars, and
supernovas, which helps us ⓑto better understand

through their hobbies, such as amateur programmers
developing
new
technologies,
amateur
writers
publishing their work in local magazines, amateur

primary (D)motivation. Other people enjoy hobbies
for the communities ⓒwhere they can become a

contributions to society through their hobbies,

them, that makes a hobby ⓓrewarding and fun.
