다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the U.S.
Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a (A)[monotonous
/ varied] range of landscapes, from hot desert regions
to great mountain ranges. It takes about five months
for the average person to walk through the trail,
which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually
start in early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with a
low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting
a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the PCT.
In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. Hikers cook their own
meals, and sometimes they have to endure days
without eating. Securing water is another (B)[minor
/ crucial] requirement because not all the water
sources are safe to drink. Hikers are advised to
carry the latest PCT Water Report, a list of all water
sources. When it comes to sleeping, most hikers sleep
in tents, and in some areas, they can use shelters to
stay safe from the harsh weather. If you are lucky,
you may find “trail angels,” who provide transportation
to close towns, meals, or other forms of assistance.
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was (C)[demanding / effortless], it
was also a gift. It allowed me to see what I am
truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you meet
along the way. The trail has led to lasting friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance to
see the magnificent landscapes of the American West.
(A)
(B)             (C)
choices: monotonous     crucialdemanding
varied     crucialeffortless
monotonous     minoreffortless
varied     crucialdemanding
varied     minordemanding
solution: (A) 앞에서 PCT는 세 개의 주와 일곱 개의 국립 공원을 통과한다 고 했고, 뒤에서 뜨거운 사막 지대부터 웅장한 산맥까지 경험할 수 있다고 했으므로 다양한 풍경이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 varied(다양한)가 적절하다. (B) 자연에서 수개월 동안 생활해야 하며 모든 수원이 마실 수 있는 것은 아니라고 했으므로, 물을 확보하는 것은 매우 중요하 다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 crucial(필수적인)이 적절하다. (C) 앞에서 낮은 완주율, 식수 확보의 어려움, 가혹한 날씨 등을 언 급했으며, ‘~이지만’을 뜻하는 접속사 While이 쓰였으므로 주절에서 언급한 ‘선물(gift)’과 대조되는 의미의 demanding(힘든)이 적절하다.

Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
What Is the PCT?
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person to walk through the trail, which is
known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually start in
early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with
a low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers
attempting a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the
PCT.

the attractions and challenges of long-distancehiking through the PCT

the geographical features of the PCT and essentialhiking precautions

While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a basic level, which was simply to “Set sail, make
it fast, no thoughts of energy or speed, lean back,
let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water (A)[what /
that] mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place (B)[which / where] he could
be completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named
his boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after
the
apparent
meaninglessness
of
his
sailing
adventures. (C)[Watching / Watch] the waves while
on his boat, Einstein forgot all his worries. Like
Einstein, for many people, hobbies just provide the
conditions for a sense of pure satisfaction.

(B)
(C)

thatwhich      Watching
thatwhere      Watch

thatwhere      Watching
solution: (A) 주어 자리의 it, 동사 was와 함께 동명사구 ‘being out on the water(물 위에 나가 있는 것)’를 강조하는 ‘it is[was] ~ that …(…한 것은 바로 ~이다[이었다])’ 형태의 ‘it - that’ 강조구 문을 이루어야 하므로 that이 적절하다. (B) 완전한 절(he ~ relaxed)을 이끌어 선행사 a place를 수식하 는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다. (C) 콤마(,) 뒤의 완전한 절(Einstein ~ worries)과 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며 주어 Einstein이 ‘보는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Watching이 적절 하다.

You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.
That is, it sometimes leads to an unexpected
contribution to society. For example, Thomas Bopp,
a manager at a construction materials factory and
an amateur astronomer, discovered the comet
Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his friends
in the Arizona desert. To make the story even more
shocking, he was using a borrowed telescope that
his friend had assembled himself. And Bopp is not
alone.
Numerous
amateur
astronomers
have
discovered comets, stars, and supernovas, which
helps us to better understand the solar system and
the universe. Amateurs in many other fields have
made important contributions through their hobbies,
such as amateur programmers developing new
technologies, amateur writers publishing their work
in local magazines, amateur history researchers
preserving historical sites ... The list goes on and on!

Discoveries made by non-professional astronomershave played an important role in expanding ourknowledge of the universe.
The positive social impact of hobbies can be foundin various fields other than astronomy, includingtechnology and history.

For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If you meet someone who has woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer are titles that people are proud to call themselves. they offer no room for growth or self-improvement

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

Hobbies Are Modern Activities
Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do
in their free time. In the past, though, this probably
wasn’t true because most people had to work long
hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time
must have been hard to come by. However, the
Industrial Revolution and the labor movement that
followed it led to a gradual decrease in working
hours to eight-hour work days and five-day work
weeks. For the first time in history, a majority of
people had free time to enjoy activities that they
found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure
may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it
takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a
hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful
effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome
hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If
you meet someone who has woken up at the crack
of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you
can assume that they think of themselves as a
“photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer
are titles that people are proud to call themselves. On
the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV
watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing
online aren’t considered serious hobbies because
there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.
choices: These days, everyone has their own activity thatthey enjoy doing when they are not working.
The Industrial Revolution and the labor movementcontributed to shorter working hours.
The reduction in working hours gradually gavemore people the chance to enjoy meaningfulactivities outside their jobs.
A serious hobby involves trying to develop one'sabilities rather than simply enjoying an activity.
An activity can still be regarded as a serioushobby even if it offers neither challenge norpersonal development.

Hobbies Create Community
J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
(A) He wrote of the isolation that he and other people who loved languages experienced: “But they become shy, ashamed of spending the valuable commodity of time for their private pleasure, and higher developments are locked in secret places.” Things are very different now.
(B) He invented languages with grammar rules and histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former inspired by Welsh, and the latter inspired by Finnish and Latin. But inventing languages was a frustrating hobby because he had to isolate himself while creating them.
(C) The Internet allows people to learn about languages and meet other language enthusiasts from all over the world. Instead of working on their projects in private, they can easily find other like-minded people to share their passion, celebrate their achievements, and encourage each other along the way. They could even work together on language projects that Tolkien may have never been able to imagine.

What Is the PCT?
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person (A)[walks / to walk] through the
trail, which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers”
usually start in early spring and head north,
(B)[arrive / arriving] at their destination in early
winter. It’s a hard journey with a low completion
rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting a thru-hiking
(C)[succeed / to succeed] in finishing the PCT.

In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. Hikers cook their own
meals, and sometimes they have to endure days
without eating. Securing water is another crucial
requirement because not all the water sources are
safe to drink. Hikers are advised to carry the latest
PCT Water Report, a list of all water sources. When
it comes to sleeping, most hikers sleep in tents,
and in some areas, they can use shelters to stay
safe from the harsh weather. If you are lucky, you
may find “trail angels,” who provide transportation
to close towns, meals, or other forms of assistance.
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to see the magnificent landscapes of the American
West.

While some people pursue a hobby to improve

Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he was
18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long

physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care

completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his

hobbies just provide the conditions for a sense of
pure satisfaction.

body:
Hobbies Are Modern Activities
Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do
in their free time. In the past, though, this probably
wasn’t true because most people had to work long
hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time
must have been hard to come by. (A)____________,
the Industrial Revolution and the labor ⓐmovement
that followed it led to a gradual decrease in
working hours to eight-hour work days and five-day
work weeks. For the first time in history, a majority
of people had free time to enjoy activities that they
found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are ⓑserious. Serious
leisure may sound like a ⓒcontradiction, but that’s
what it takes for an activity to ⓓqualify as a
hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to
make a meaningful effort to improve your skills,
take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better
version of yourself. If you meet someone who has
woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at
the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think
of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a
gamer, or a photographer are ⓔtitles that people
are proud to call themselves. (B)____________, you
wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online
surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t
considered serious hobbies because there’s no
challenge or way to improve yourself.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Hobbies Can Contribute
You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.
That is, it sometimes leads to a(n) (A)[predictable /
unexpected] contribution to society. For example,
Thomas
Bopp,
a
manager
at
a
construction
materials
factory
and
an
amateur
astronomer,
discovered the comet Hale-Bopp while observing
the sky with his friends in the Arizona desert. To
make the story even more shocking, he was using
a borrowed telescope that his friend had assembled
himself. And Bopp is not alone. Numerous amateur
astronomers have discovered comets, stars, and
supernovas, which helps us to better understand the
solar system and the universe. Amateurs in many
other fields have made important contributions
through
their
hobbies,
such
as
amateur
programmers developing new technologies, amateur
writers publishing their work in local magazines,
amateur history researchers preserving historical
sites ... The list goes on and on!
There are many reasons why people pursue
hobbies. For many people, the challenge of learning
a new skill or achieving a difficult goal is their
primary (B)[motivation / discouragement]. Other
people enjoy hobbies for the communities they can
become a part of or the friendships they can make
there. Still others enjoy hobbies because they can
lose track of time and be in the moment, similar to
being in a (C)[distracted / meditative] state. Some
people even end up making contributions to society
through their hobbies, oftentimes unexpectedly. It is
the physical, mental, or emotional experience, or
even a combination of them, that makes a hobby
rewarding and fun. Perhaps it should be called
“pleisure.”
(A)
(B)               (C)

There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.
The sports community is optimistic that it can reduce
its environmental impact by taking two main steps:
ⓐtransitioning to more sustainable operations before,
during, and after events and ⓑraising awareness
among the public about their impact. Efforts to adopt
more responsible approaches have been made by
various organizations, and the International Olympic
Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a
good example. The IOC set up the Sport and
Environment Commission decades ago and ⓒdeclared
the
environment
as
essential
to
the
Olympic
Movement, in addition to sports and culture. It has
since encouraged host nations to adopt more
environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.
As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000
Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s
largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt
Lake City Winter Olympics ⓓadopted a new energy
recycling system which used the curling hall’s air
conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms
in the ⓔvenue. Also, for the 2010 Vancouver Winter
Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating venue was built
with salvaged timber. (A)한때 오염되었던 산업 대지
위에 지어진 2012년 런던 하계 올림픽의 ‘올림픽 파크‘는
유럽에서 가장 큰 도시 공원으로 탈바꿈되었다. Then
at the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, electricity was
generated with hydrogen instead of fossil fuel,
which supplied power for many residential buildings
in the Olympic Village and Paralympic Village.

On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook
the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf
of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea before
it was eventually halted. Despite continuing restoration
efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered.
(A) When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are
attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As
they grow, they release enzymes that break
down oil into carbon dioxide and water.
(B) One approach to addressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration
method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments
and possess the capability to break down
various components of oil.
(C) Although this process may take several weeks or
months, it represents a more sustainable method
of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional
approaches involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean,
some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their
growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of
breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes
that break down plastic into smaller molecules,
ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water.

body:
Many sporting events have a negative impact on
the environment because they require massive
structures to host them. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring
greater amounts of building materials for construction.
Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a
construction site, there is a loss of nature. Every ton
of
concrete
and
steel
used
in
the
building
foundation and structure is produced, transported,
poured, and put together by equipment and facilities
that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere.
Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts
of water, electricity, and other forms of resources
are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. (A) For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. (B) As
long as the competition is on, the track needs to
be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. (C) Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. (D) During the event,
spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the
plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they
consumed leave trash cans overflowing. (E) After the
event has ended, in addition to the significant
amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the
effects those people caused and the emissions
generated from their travel continue to have a
lasting negative impact on air quality.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: challenges in maintaining optimal conditions forwinter sports facilities
the need to build eco-friendly stadiums to protectthe environment
the environmental consequences of hosting majorsporting events
how sporting facilities are constructed andmaintained
the economic and social costs of running sportingevents

unlike disposable plastic bags.

only effective if they are used more than 7,100
times.

W: Of course. That means you’d have to utilize the
same bag every day for 20 years.
M: Wow! Then, should I give up and go back to
disposable plastic bags?
W: Not necessarily. Just remember to use reusable
bags as often as you can.
M: Okay. I’ll use the ones I have until they fall
apart.
W: Good idea. It’s important to put sustainability
into practice in our daily lives.

There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.
The sports community is optimistic that it can
reduce its environmental impact by taking two main
steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations
before,
during,
and
after
events
and
raising
awareness among the public about their impact.
Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have
been made by various organizations, and the
International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading
the way by setting a good example. The IOC set
up the Sport and Environment Commission decades
ago and declared the environment as essential to
the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and
culture. It has since encouraged host nations to
adopt more environmental approaches to putting
on the Olympics.
As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000
Sydney Summer Olympics ⓐbecoming the world’s
largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt
Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy
recycling system ⓑwhich used the curling hall’s air
conditioning
unit
to
heat
the
showers
and
bathrooms
in
the
venue.
Also, for the 2010
Vancouver Winter Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating
venue was built with ⓒsalvaged timber. The Olympic
Park for the 2012 London Summer Olympics,
ⓓwhat was built on industrial land that was once
contaminated, was converted to the biggest urban
park in Europe. Then at the 2020 Tokyo Summer
Olympics, electricity was ⓔgenerated with hydrogen
instead of fossil fuel, which supplied power for
many residential buildings in the Olympic Village
and Paralympic Village.

overflowing. After the event has ended, in addition
to the significant amount of trash that needs to be
disposed of, the effects ⓒ[that / what] those
people caused and the emissions generated from
their travel continue to have a lasting negative
impact on air quality.

Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool for universally raising awareness about environmental responsibility. choices: extensive – discourage
limited – foster
extensive – promote
limited – promote

solution:
1. 스포츠는 인기가 높아 수십억 명에게 영향을 미치고(광범위한 인기), 유명 선수·코치가 팬의 환경 의식을 높인다고 했다.
2. 팬들은 환경 캠페인을 잘 받아들이고 생활 습관을 바꿀 의향이 있다고 했으므로 스포츠는 친환경적 생활 변화를 ‘촉진’한다.
3. (A)에는 extensive(광범위한), (B)에는 promote(촉진하다)가 알맞다. limited는 인기가 ‘제한적’이라는 뜻이라 틀리고, discourage는 반대 방향이다.
따라서 답은 ③이다.

W: Hi, today I’m excited to introduce a place I
recently visited during my summer vacation: the
Aral Sea.
(A) The Aral Sea serves as an example of how human
actions can have destructive environmental impacts.
I’m worried that other parts of the world may
also suffer from this kind of ecological collapse.
(B) Sadly, however, as of 2007, it had substantially
declined to 10% of its original size due to the
construction of dams and canals for cotton
farming. The decline not only damaged local
water resources but also induced changes in the
local climate, resulting in extended summers and
dry days.
(C) It is located in Central Asia, between Uzbekistan
and Kazakhstan. The Aral Sea, meaning “sea of
islands” in Kazakh, is not a sea but a saltwater
lake that was once the world’s fourth-largest lake.
We should be mindful of the impact of our choices.

위 주어진 담화에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 여자가 최근 여름방학 동안 방문한 아랄해를 소개하게 되어 기쁘다고 말하는 주어진 담화 뒤에, 아랄해의 위치와 명칭의 의미, 그리고 과거 세계에서 네 번째로 큰 염수호였다는 기본 적인 배경 정보를 설명하는 (C), Sadly, however(그러나 안타깝 게도)를 통해 과거와 현재를 대비하며, 댐과 운하 건설로 인해 호수의 면적이 원래의 10% 수준으로 줄어들었고 그 결과 지 역의 기후까지 변화했다는 내용을 설명하는 (B), 아랄해의 사 례가 인간의 행동이 환경에 파괴적인 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 보여 주는 대표적인 예임을 언급하고, 이러한 생태계 붕괴가 다른 지역에서도 발생할 수 있다는 화자의 우려를 나타내는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
[1]
Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the
possibility that nearly one in every four English
soccer stadiums could be partially or completely
flooded in the near future due to climate change
and extreme weather events. Some research even
predicted that by 2050 almost half of the cities that
once hosted the Winter Olympics would not be
able to do so again for lack of snow and ice. Also,
the US Open Tennis Championships organizers
implemented an “extreme heat policy,” having
mandatory short breaks for players to cool down
during matches, after a few quit their matches due
to extreme heat. As more sports are affected by
climate change, concerns are growing.
[2]
_________________________________, however. The sports
community is optimistic that it can reduce its
environmental impact by taking two main steps:
transitioning to more sustainable operations before,
during, and after events and raising awareness among
the public about their impact. Efforts to adopt more
responsible approaches have been made by various
organizations, and the International Olympic Committee
(IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example.
The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission
decades ago and declared the environment as
essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to
sports and culture. It has since encouraged host
nations to adopt more environmental approaches to
putting on the Olympics.

Too many cooks spoil the broth
It is no use crying over spilled milk
Where there is a will, there is a way
There is light at the end of the tunnel

(C) 시간 부사절 접속사 while(~하면서) 뒤에 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 절이 와야 하나 뒤에 명사구 less energy만 있으므로, 접속 사 뒤에 ‘주어+be동사’가 생략된 ‘접속사+분사’ 구문을 이루는 분 사 형태가 되어야 한다. 생략된 주어 a cultivation environment(배 양 환경)가 ‘태우는[소비하는]’ 주체이고 뒤의 명사구가 목적어에 해 당하므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 burning이 적절하다. 지학사(신상근) 2과

have your own delicious homemade dressing!

you go! You can add beans or cheese if you

미래 작물인 엔셋(enset)이 번성하는 지역이기도 하다.

relative of the banana. The fruit of the plant isn’t
safe to eat, but the stems and roots can be
processed and used to make bread. Approximately
20 million people (A)[rely on / do without] this
plant for food in Ethiopia, but it is almost unknown
outside of the country. Scientists anticipate that this

million people in a warming world, establishing

fiber, vitamins, and other nutrients. Cacti’s ability to
thrive in dry and harsh environments makes them a
(B)[crucial / dispensable] crop in the face of climate
change.

Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety
of dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks.

China, but it is becoming more common in other
parts of the world. Seaweed, gaining attention for
(C)[aggravating / addressing] soil degradation, is

(B) 북미와 남미 사막 지역이 원산지인 선인장은 라틴아메리카의 주요 식량이며, 건조하고 혹독한 환경에서 잘 자라 기후 변화에 ‘중 요한’ 작물이라는 흐름이 알맞으므로, crucial(중요한)이 적절하다. (C) 전 세계의 바위 암석 해안을 따라 주로 번성하는 식물로, 식이 섬유, 필수 비타민 및 미네랄이 풍부해 많은 건강상 이점을 제공하 는 해조류가 주목받는 또 다른 이유로 토양 황폐화 문제를 ‘해결하 는 것(addressing)’을 위해 주목받는다는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

As our planet faces increasing environmental
challenges and climate change, there is growing
interest in eco-friendly foods that have less impact
on the environment. The following foods eaten in
various regions of the world are gaining attention
as sustainable foods for the future.
False Bananas
ⓐ에티오피아는 그것의 커피 재배로 유명한데, 유망한
미래 작물인 엔셋(enset)이 번성하는 지역이기도 하다.
Enset, also known as “false banana,” is a close
relative of the banana. The fruit of the plant isn’t
safe to eat, but the stems and roots can be
processed and used to make bread. Approximately
20 million people (A)[rely on / do without] this
plant for food in Ethiopia, but it is almost unknown
outside of the country. Scientists anticipate that this
crop has the potential to feed more than 100
million people in a warming world, establishing
itself as a new fundamental food for the future.
Cacti
Native to the deserts of both North and South
America, cacti are a fundamental food in Latin
American communities, where the flat pads are
often stirred and served with eggs or in salads and
tacos. There are over 1,500 species of cacti, and
many of them are safe to eat. Cacti are rich in
fiber, vitamins, and other nutrients. Cacti’s ability to
thrive in dry and harsh environments makes them a
(B)[crucial / dispensable] crop in the face of climate
change.
Seaweed
Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety
of dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks.
Seaweed is mostly eaten in Korea, Japan, and
China, but it is becoming more common in other
parts of the world. Seaweed, gaining attention for
(C)[aggravating / addressing] soil degradation, is
packed with fiber, essential vitamins, and minerals,
offering numerous health benefits.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Growing environmental and climate challengesare driving interest in sustainable foods.
Enset, often called the “false banana,” is closelyrelated to bananas, but its fruit is inedible.
Scientists foresee enset becoming a staple foodcapable of feeding over 100 million people in awarming world.
Indigenous to the deserts of North and SouthAmerica, cacti serve as a main food across LatinAmerican communities.
Seaweed is rarely consumed in Korea, Japan,and China and is sufficient in essential vitamins.

Host: I see. I heard some people are against
lab-grown meat, even though it tastes like
real meat and can reduce damage to animals
and the environment.
Dr. Perry: Yes, that’s correct. Two main issues are
pointed out. First, there is criticism that
growing meat in a lab requires a significant
amount of energy, so it’s not as environmentally
friendly as lab-grown meat companies claim.
(A) It is expected that technological advances will
reduce these problems. For example, the cells
can even be extracted from eggs or feathers of
chickens, and some companies are replacing
culture media made from animals with media
made from plants.
(B) There is also criticism that it won’t eliminate
animal cruelty 100%. This is because the process
extracts cells from animals, although it doesn’t
kill them. Also, there have been continuing
concerns about the cruelty associated with
producing the culture medium. For honest
animal welfare, these processes must be carried
out ethically to minimize the suffering caused
to animals.
(C) Of course, traditional livestock farming emits
significantly more greenhouse gases than the
cultured meat industry does. Simplifying the
production process and using renewable energy
will address many of these concerns.

Host: Welcome to News Tonight. What was once
the stuff of science fiction is finally arriving
on our dinner plates. We’re talking about
lab-grown meat. You may be reluctant to try

you, Dr. Perry. Can you tell our viewers what
kind of research you are currently conducting?
Dr. Perry: Thank you for having me, Kelly. I am
currently leading a lab-grown meat project
research team. Our team is working to trace
the process of cell division and growth in
lab-grown meat, with the goal of discovering
a cultivation environment that enables the
creation of a better texture while burning
less energy.
Host: I see. Now let’s dive into our main topic,
lab-grown meat. First, tell us (B)_______________
_______________________________________.
Dr. Perry: Lab-grown meat refers to meat grown
from cells we keep alive in a controlled
environment. It is different from conventional
beef or chicken, which is produced by raising
and
slaughtering
farm
animals.
It’s
also
different
from
plant-based
meat,
which
derives its protein solely from plants. It is
often called cultured or cultivated meat, too.
Host: I’m sure many people are wondering about
the reasons for developing lab-grown meat.
Dr. Perry: Every year, 80 billion animals are
slaughtered for meat. The livestock industry
uses 83% of the world’s farming land and
produces 60% of agricultural greenhouse gas
emissions.
Since
lab-grown
meat
doesn’t
require killing animals, it reduces carbon
emissions, and it retains the same nutrition
and flavor as regular meat. This makes it an
attractive substitute.

tests (A)[has yielded / have yielded] positive
reviews. Many taste testers were unable to
taste a difference between lab-grown and
regular meat. Some of them even guessed
incorrectly which sample was lab-grown.
Host: I see, but why do we need lab-grown meat
when we already have plant-based meat?

but some people still feel that it does not
quite match the taste, texture, and overall
eating
experience
of
real
animal
meat.
Lab-grown meat can provide people with a
product that is biologically identical to real
meat in a way that’s much less harmful to
the planet and animals.

idea of lab-grown meat will also wonder
(B)[what / if] it’s safe.

Singapore in 2020, and more recently, the
U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the
U.S. Department of Agriculture have also
approved the sale of lab-grown chicken.

is probably safe. It’s hoped that the safety of
cultured
meat

improve
with

collect more data over a long period of time

Host: Welcome to News Tonight. What was once
the stuff of science fiction is finally arriving
on our dinner plates. We’re talking about
lab-grown meat. You may be reluctant to try
it. However strange it may seem, many
people say it tastes just like regular meat,
and it has big advantages for preventing
animal
suffering
and
reducing
pollution.
Today, we have tissue engineering expert Dr.
Mike Perry with us to learn more about
lab-grown meat. It’s an honor to meet you,
Dr. Perry. Can you tell our viewers what kind
of research you are currently conducting?
Dr. Perry: Thank you for having me, Kelly. I am
currently leading a lab-grown meat project
research team. Our team is working to trace
the process of cell division and growth in
lab-grown meat, with the goal of discovering
a cultivation environment that enables the
creation of a better texture while burning
less energy.
Host: I see. Now let’s dive into our main topic,
lab-grown meat. First, tell us what lab-grown
meat is.
Dr. Perry: Lab-grown meat refers to meat grown
from cells we keep alive in a controlled
environment. It is different from conventional
beef or chicken, which is produced by raising
and
slaughtering
farm
animals.
It’s
also
different
from
plant-based
meat,
which
derives its protein solely from plants. It is
often called cultured or cultivated meat, too.
Host: I’m sure many people are wondering about
the reasons for developing lab-grown meat.
Dr. Perry: Every year, 80 billion animals are
slaughtered for meat. The livestock industry
uses 83% of the world’s farming land and
produces 60% of agricultural greenhouse gas
emissions. Since lab-grown meat doesn’t
require killing animals, it reduces carbon
emissions, and it retains the same nutrition
and flavor as regular meat. This makes it an
attractive substitute.

Many people claim that lab-grown meat closelyresembles conventional meat while helping curbanimal suffering and pollution.
Dr. Mike Perry’s team is investigating how cellsdivide and grow in lab-grown meat.
Lab-grown meat is distinct from plant-basedmeat made solely from plants.
Lab-grown meat serves as an appealing substitutefor conventional meat that differs in terms ofnutrition and taste.

begins with the extraction of cells from a
living animal’s muscle or skin tissue. We then
determine which cells can be multiplied to
form delicious meat products. From there, we
place the cells in a culture medium. This is a
clean and controlled environment that offers
the necessary nutrients for cells to replicate
and mature by themselves. When the meat is
ready, it is harvested and processed like a
regular meat product.

when we already have plant-based meat?

Host: I see. Now let’s dive into our main topic, lab-grown meat. First, tell us what lab-grown meat is.
Dr. Perry: Lab-grown meat refers to meat grown from cells that we have kept alive in a controlled environment. It is different from conventional beef or chicken, which is produced by raising and slaughtering farm animals. It’s also different from plant-based meat, which derives its protein solely from plants. It is often called cultured or cultivated meat, too.

characteristic of universal design. A door with a
lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or

difficulties may struggle to open a tightly

body:
Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Necessity of a Common Language for Efficient Information Delivery
Why Foreign Travelers Need Visual Symbols and Braille in Modern Elevators
Universal Design for Accessible Information Across Languages and Sensory Abilities
How the Advancement of Technology Makes Information Access More Convenient
The Role of Electronic Boards and Voice Announcements in Public Transportation

4. 따라서 답은 ③이다.

fundamental
aspect
of

Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but

playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who cannot participate in the intended
manner ⓐfeeling excluded.
For children with disabilities, play is even more
crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social
skills.

the
conventional
design
of
playgrounds does not typically accommodate their
needs, either ⓑoverwhelm or boring them. A visit
to
a
standard
playground
with

with

ⓒthat fail to satisfy everyone.
Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and ⓓconnect with
nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging
design task. By involving children with disabilities
and their families in the design process and
creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge
ⓔthat
play
is
more
than
just
a source
of
enjoyment. This approach results in spaces where
people of all abilities, ages, and languages can take

Universal design also ensures that an environment
or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should
be able to use a design regardless of who they are
and what they’re capable of, and no one should be
excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without
curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard
time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers
not only for wheelchair users but also for people
moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts,
automatic doors in public buildings also allow all
people to enter without any major problems.
Another
characteristic
of
universal
design
is
requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks
to create products that can be used efficiently and
comfortably without (A)[cause / causing] unnecessary
fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble
trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck.
Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people
with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand
or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever
opening devices have been designed. A lever-type
door handle, which requires no firm grip or
twisting, is also an example (B)[that / what] reflects
this characteristic of universal design. A door with a
lever-type door handle can be opened (C)[using /
used] an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits
people carrying baskets as well as those with
limited strength in their hands.

(B)
(C)

solution: (A) 전치사 without의 목적어 자리이며, 뒤에 명사구 unnecessary fatigue가 이어지므로 목적어를 취할 수 있는 능동형 동명사 causing이 적절하다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(reflects ~ design)을 이끌어 선행 사 an example을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (C) 완전한 절(A door ~ opened)에 접속사나 주어 없이 이어 지며 주절의 동작(can be opened)과 ‘팔꿈치나 오므린 손을 사용하는 것(using an elbow or a closed hand)‘이 동시에 일 어나는 부대상황을 나타내므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리 이다. 뒤에 목적어(an elbow or a closed hand)가 이어지므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 using이 적절하다.

Play

fundamental
aspect
of
human
development that continues all through our lives.
Playgrounds serve as a central place for play, but
many individuals struggle to fully engage in these
spaces due to their restrictive arrangements. Often,
playgrounds are designed to satisfy specific types of
play or particular age groups, which can leave
children who cannot participate in the intended
manner feeling excluded.
For children with disabilities, play is even more
crucial as it offers an opportunity to practice social
skills.

the
conventional
design
of
playgrounds does not typically accommodate their
needs, either overwhelming or boring them. A visit
to
a
standard
playground
with
children
with

Playgrounds should be designed to foster social
connections for all ages, provide sensory stimulation,
encourage physical exercise, and connect with
nature. Achieving this integration is a challenging
design task. By involving children with disabilities
and their families in the design process and
creating friendlier playgrounds, we can acknowledge
that play is more than just a source of enjoyment.
This approach results in spaces where people of all
abilities, ages, and languages can take part in the
joy of play.

For example, Martin’s Park, designed by Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, is a universally designed playground. Unusual play structures and a large ship provide endless experiences of play that can engage every child. The various methods of play have different means of access, allowing kids who are able to scramble up hills, while children who can’t walk can use the sloping paths to reach the top. Interpretive signs point out the inclusive routes and elements of the playground. The inclusion of more than 1,000 trees grants children and adults the chance to experience the sensory aspects of plants.
Play isn’t just for kids anymore. Senior play spaces and public exercise equipment are being installed around the world. Play spaces for older adults provide health benefits and encourage engagement with their families and community. Hence, playgrounds need to be redesigned as spaces where everyone can enjoy themselves.

[요약문] As a universally designed playground, Martin's Park offers (A)____________________ in its facilities, ensuring the successful (B)____________________ of diverse individuals across generations.

solution: ⓑ access and use → to access and (to) use (동사 make, 가목 적어 it, 목적격보어 possible, 의미상 주어 for them과 함께 ‘-가 ~하는 것을 …하게 만들다’의 의미를 갖는 ‘make+it(가목적어)+목 적격보어(형용사)+for+의미상 주어+to부정사(진목적어)’의 구조로, ‘가목적어-진목적어’ 구문을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 진목적어 자리 이자 ‘for+목적어(them)‘의 형태로 의미상주어를 취하고 있으므로, access and use를 accessing and using이 아니라 to부정사구 to access and (to) use로 고친다. 참고로 to부정사가 병렬 연결될 때 to는 생략 가능하므로 to use 또는 use 모두 가능하다.)

or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should
be able to use a design regardless of who they are
and what they’re capable of, and no one should be
excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without
curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard

automatic doors in public buildings also allow all
people to enter without any major problems.

body:
Addario’s career took a significant turn when she
went to Afghanistan in 2000. Her photographs
captured the grief, resilience, and courage of
Afghan women.
(A) Time and again, however, she has risked her life
to capture images that speak volumes about the
suffering of those ⓐ[catching / caught] in the
conflicts between nations.
“The idea of me going to a war zone was out
of the question. ㉠그때 9.11 테러가 왔고, 이건
내가 취재해야 할 것만 같은 생각이 들었던 결정
적인 역사적 순간이었어요.
(B) This body of work gained international recognition,
ⓑ[served / serving] as a stepping stone for
Addario’s future achievements. Over the years,
Addario’s work has taken her to many regions
torn by war, including Iraq, Sudan, Libya, and
Syria. She knows very well what could happen in
the wars: she was captured twice and was even
threatened with her life.
(C) From there I ended up covering the war in Iraq
in 2003 because again, I felt like I needed to
be there. Young soldiers of my generation were
going in to fight, and I thought it was
important to document the war. I’m lucky
because I’ve survived. I’m now at the point in
my life and my career ⓒ[which / where] many
of my friends are not. And so I think it’s
important to realize there is a reason I’m still
here, and I have to keep pushing forward.”

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 주어진 글에서 Addario가 2000년 아프가니스탄에 가서 아프간 여성들의 사진을 찍었다고 했으므로, 그 작업(This body of work)이 국제적 인정을 받아 이후 여러 전쟁 지역으로 이어졌 고 두 번 붙잡히는 등 위험을 겪었다는 내용의 (B)가 먼저 이 어진다. (B)에서 전쟁에서 벌어질 수 있는 위험을 언급한 뒤, however로 그럼에도 목숨을 걸고 사진을 담아 왔다는 (A)가 이어지며, (A) 끝에서 9.11 테러가 결정적 순간이었다고 언급한 다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 From there(그곳에서부터)로 이어받아 2003년 이라크 전쟁을 취재하게 된 이야기와 계속 나아가야 한다는 다짐으로 마무리된다. 따라서 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)이다.

body:
I have found that nothing in life is of value (A)[if /
unless] you take risks. Nothing. Now I’m sure in
your experiences in school, in applying to college,
in picking your major, in deciding what you want to
do with life, people have told you to make sure
you have something to “fall back on.” But I never
understood that concept, having something to fall
back on. If I’m going to fall, I don’t want to fall
back on anything. I want to fall forward. This is
what I mean. Reggie Jackson struck out 2,600 times
in his career, the most in the history of baseball.
But you don’t hear about it. People remember the
home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 (B)[failed / successful] experiments because
the 1,001st was the light bulb. Fall forward. Every
failed experiment is one step closer to success.
You’ve got to take risks. I want to talk to you
about why that’s so important. You will fail at some
point in your lives. You will lose. You will embarrass
yourselves. There is no doubt about it. I know
that’s probably not a traditional message for a
graduation ceremony but I’m telling you. Embrace it
because it’s (C)[avoidable / inevitable].

body:
In the acting business, you fail all the time. Early
on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact that I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just
getting smaller and smaller. I didn’t get the job. But
here’s the thing. I didn’t quit. I didn’t fall back. I
walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So
you will catch a break, which is exactly what I did.
Last year I did a play called Fences on Broadway. It
was at the Court Theater. It was at the same
theater that I failed that first audition 30 years
prior. The point is every graduate here today has
the training and the talent to succeed. But do you
have _____________________________?

body:
In the acting business, you fail all the time. Early
on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact that I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just
getting smaller and smaller. I didn’t get the job. But
here’s the thing. I didn’t quit. I didn’t fall back. I
walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So
you will catch a break, which is exactly what I did.
Last year I did a play called Fences on Broadway. It
was at the Court Theater. It was at the same
theater that I failed that first audition 30 years
prior. The point is every graduate here today has
the training and the talent to succeed. But do you
have _____________________________?

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The speaker once auditioned for a Broadway musical despite being unable to sing well.
Hearing the man ahead of him sing made the speaker feel less confident before his audition.
After failing the audition, the speaker decided to stop trying for roles on Broadway.
The speaker kept preparing for more auditions even after experiencing repeated failures.
Years later, the speaker performed at the same theater where he had failed an audition decades earlier.
solution:
1. 화자는 노래를 못하는데도 브로드웨이 뮤지컬 오디션을 봤고(①), 앞사람이 파바로티처럼 노래하자 점점 작아졌다(②).
2. 떨어진 뒤에도 그만두지 않고 다음 오디션을 계속 준비했다(④).
3. 30년 뒤 처음 오디션에서 떨어진 바로 그 극장에서 연극을 했다(⑤).
4. ③ ‘실패 후 브로드웨이 배역 도전을 그만두기로 했다’는 ‘I didn’t quit.’와 어긋난다.
따라서 답은 ③이다.

the college’s website and see what courses are
offered.

that soon.

how to prepare for the interview.

body:
Researcher and professor Carol Dweck uses the
term mindset to describe the way people think
about ability and talent. Dweck describes two
different mindsets. One is a fixed mindset, which
suggests
that
your
abilities
are
inherent
and
unchangeable. The other is a growth mindset, which
views them as something you can improve through
practice. There are several differences between these
two mindsets. First, in a fixed mindset, you view
failure as permanent, but with a growth mindset,
you see failure as a chance to learn. Second, those
with a fixed mindset are more likely to view
negative feedback as a personal attack, while those
with a growth mindset will see it as a chance to
improve. Lastly, those with a fixed mindset are likely
to give up when they face an obstacle. Meanwhile,
those with a growth mindset will view obstacles as
a chance to experiment and solve problems.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how to overcome failure using a growth mindset
key differences between permanent failure andtemporary failure
how fixed and growth mindsets shape responsesto challenges
the process of measuring a person's inborn abilityand talent
ways to teach children to develop a growth mindset

M: Have you ever heard of the Harvard study that

It followed the lives of two groups of men for

boomer children to understand how childhood
experience reaches across decades to affect
health and well-being in middle age. So what
keeps us happy and healthy as we go through

Waldinger, you’re mistaken.

relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period.

own way.”
Luca “Lazylegz” Patuelli has lived by this motto his
whole life. Born in 1984 with a rare disorder ⓐaffecting
the bones and joints of the body, he has undergone
a total of 16 surgeries since he was 7 months old,
to support his legs, hips, back, and shoulders.
Despite the physical challenges, Lazylegz learned at
an early age about ㉠____________________________. Always
eager to stay active and join his friends in any
activity, he managed to participate in activities such
as soccer, football, and baseball. He also succeeded
in learning how to rock climb and ski, and he
found ways to join his high school swim and dive
teams. As he explored the full range of physical
activities, skateboarding developed into a particular
passion for him.

challenging movements. He slowly began creating a
unique style that ⓑmade the most of his upper
body strength. By using his crutches as extensions
of his arms, Bboy Lazylegz was born!

events such as Breakin’ Convention, World of Dance,
and Hip Hop International. He created ILL-Abilities
in 2007, an international Bboy crew ⓒcomposed of

abled. “We have a message, and that message is
No excuses, no limits. We want to encourage people

went to Afghanistan in 2000. Her photographs

________________. Over the years, Addario’s work has

Iraq, Sudan, Libya, and Syria. She knows very well
what could happen in the wars: she was captured
twice and was even threatened with her life. Time
and again, however, she has risked her life to
capture images that speak volumes about the
suffering of those caught in the conflicts between
nations.
“The idea of me (B)going to a war zone was
(C)out of the question. Then came 9/11, and it was
such a defining moment in history that I felt like I
needed to cover it. From there I ended up covering
the war in Iraq in 2003 because again, I felt like I
needed
to
be
there.
Young
soldiers
of
my
generation (D)were going in to fight, and I thought
it was important to document the war. I’m lucky
because I’ve survived. I’m now at the point in my
life and my career (E)where many of my friends are
not. And so I think it’s important to realize there is
a reason I’m still here, and I have to keep pushing
forward.”

often
see
individuals

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

G: I’m planning to volunteer to make soap for
children in need. I heard that many children
suffer from diseases by not washing their hands
with soap.
B: That’s so sad. Proper hand washing should be
practiced by everyone. I want to volunteer to
make soap, too. Can I join you?
G: Why not? Let’s start this weekend. Why don’t we
meet at my house this Saturday?
B: Sure. What kind of soap do you want to make?
G: I want to make see-through soap. It’s a good
example of a nudge strategy, leading children to
regularly wash their hands.
B: See-through soap? Why was it made see-through?
G: There’s a toy inside it and you can see it.
B: Oh, that’s a clever idea. To get the toy inside,
children have to frequently wash their hands
with it.
G: Yes. That’s the point. According to a report, not
only did the soap help reduce diseases, but it
also helped children develop hand washing
habits.
B: See-through soap is more useful than I thought.
I hope more people use it.
G: I hope so, too.
choices: The girl plans to take part in a volunteeractivity that supports children in need.
The boy becomes interested in joining theactivity after hearing about the children’s healthproblems.
The soap contains a visible toy that motivateschildren to use it frequently.
A report showed that the soap improvedhygiene habits but had no effect on illness.
Both speakers hope that the special soap willbecome more widely used.

body:
You have probably received a notification from
your smartphone telling you that it is time to
exercise or move. These devices lead people to
move by sending notifications when they have been
inactive for a set amount of time. You may not
have realized it, but this is an example of a nudge.
A nudge is an intervention that gently guides
individuals
toward
a
desired
action,
without
forbidding any options. For example, if a school
wants to reduce the amount of sugary drinks that
students consume, then making them less visible
than bottled water counts as a nudge, while
banning them altogether does not.
Having been studied in the domain of behavioral
economics and marketing, nudging can be applied
to inducing people to make better or ideal
decisions.
Here
are
some
ways
nudges
have
succeeded in bringing about positive changes by
tweaking people’s choices.

people to move after a period of inactivity.
(B) Banning sugary drinks altogether is given as
an example of a nudge.
(C) Nudging has mainly been examined in fields
unrelated to human decision-making.
(D) Nudges can produce beneficial changes by
slightly adjusting the way choices are presented.
choices: F-F-T-F
T-F-F-T

A default is defined as an option that applies if
the chooser does ⓐnothing. Of course, the chooser

are effective at nudging people toward more
desirable behaviors. (A)인간은 그들이 이미 갖고 있는

하는

필요하기

Furthermore, because a default also gives the
impression that someone is ⓑrecommending this

(B)_____________________________________________________
can
automatically

people

on paper waste: it established printing on both

body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that
companies
use
to
manipulate
consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to (A)[stimulate /
prohibit] purchases. This typically comes in three
major
forms:
insufficient
quantities,
time,
or
availability. We make decisions more quickly under
pressure. The decision is then often made quite
automatically only on the basis of scarcity. After all,
no one wants to miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it easy
for you to see! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost (B)[visible / invisible] in the email. Gray print
on a dark background is rather hard to read, as is
very small print.
Dark
patterns
are
everywhere.
It
is
always
important to be aware that a company’s goals don’t
always (C)[different from / correspond with] your
own. To detect and resist dark patterns, you need
to read carefully and think before you click on a
button.

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: stimulate – visible – different from
stimulate – invisible – correspond with
prohibit – invisible – correspond with

1. (A) 수량·시간·이용 가능성을 제한해 압박 속에 빨리 결정하게 만든다는 내용이므로 인위적 희소성은 구매를 ‘자극하기(stimulate)’ 위해 쓰인다.
2. (B) 회색 글씨·아주 작은 글씨처럼 읽기 어렵게 만든다고 했으므로 구독 해지 링크는 거의 ‘보이지 않게(invisible)’ 만들어진다.
3. (C) 앞의 don’t always와 이어져 ‘기업의 목표가 항상 당신의 목표와 일치하지는 않는다’가 되어야 하므로 correspond with가 알맞다(different from은 동사가 아니어서 don’t 뒤에 올 수 없다).
따라서 답은 ②이다.

body:
Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two artists,
mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on
several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, ⓐcausing
them to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers ⓑwere being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the safety of pedestrians. The idea has been well
received and ⓒmirrored in cities of China, the U.S.,
Canada, and the UK as well.
Likewise, traffic engineers design pavement markings
on the roads that drive people ⓓto change their
behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one of
the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea. In
2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion ⓔwhich they are
speeding up, which prompts them to step on the
brakes. Chicago traffic engineers reported a 36%
reduction in crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive
curve in the first six months after painting the lines.
Since then, the Chicago Department of Transportation
has painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

What effect does the painted 3D crosswalk haveon motorists?
In which cities of China, the U.S., Canada, andthe UK has the idea been adopted?

How do the pavement markings in Chicagoencourage drivers to change their behavior?

Forced Continuity

body:
A default is defined as an option that applies if
the chooser does nothing. Of course, the chooser
has the freedom to opt out of the default. Defaults
are effective at nudging people toward more
desirable behaviors. Human beings are subject to a
powerful desire ㉠_____________________________________
because making a change requires a conscious
effort. Furthermore, because a default also gives the
impression that someone is recommending this
choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel
they are not being good citizens, particularly in the
case of green defaults.
Setting
greener
choices
as
defaults
can
automatically nudge people into more sustainable
behaviors. In 2008, Rutgers University instituted a
new student printing policy to save on paper waste:
it established printing on both sides of paper as
the default setting for all its printers. As a result of
that simple change, the university saved about 62
million sheets of paper in about three years.
Nudging through defaults can also apply to a
food delivery app. A company recently announced
an update for its app where it would change the
default settings for the optional items, such as
forks, spoons, and straws. Users would have to opt
out of the default to get them. The company
mentioned in an online post that ⓐhas surveyed
many of its customers, they found that more than
90% of them didn’t really need disposable plastic
items with their orders.
Are you interested in changing certain people’s
behavior? Then why not nudge them in the right
direction? There are many ways to subtly influence
people to make better decisions. As we are all
choice architects every now and then, ⓑit pays
knowing how to set people on the right path.

윗글의 빈칸 ㉠에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to value one’s own opinion
to earn a reward for their choice
to stick with what they already have
to be reluctant to follow social norms
to distrust choices recommended by others
solution: 디폴트가 사람들을 보다 바람직한 행동으로 유도하는데 효과 적인 이유 중 하나로, 빈칸 뒤에 변화하는 것은 의식적인 노력 이 필요하기 때문이라는 이유가 이어지므로 인간은 기존 상태 를 그대로 유지하려는 경향이 강하다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가 야 한다. 따라서 인간이 가진 강한 성향으로 빈칸에 들어갈 말 은 ❸ ‘이미 갖고 있는 것을 고수하려는’이 적절하다.

body:
Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two
artists, mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk
on several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them
to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
㉠______________, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers were being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the (A)[risk / safety] of pedestrians. The idea has
been well received and mirrored in cities of China,
the U.S., Canada, and the UK as well.
㉡______________, traffic engineers design pavement
markings on the roads that drive people to change
their behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one
of the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea.
In 2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion that they are
(B)[speeding up / slowing down], which prompts
them to step on the brakes. Chicago traffic
engineers reported a 36% (C)[surge / reduction] in
crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive curve in the
first six months after painting the lines. Since then,
the Chicago Department of Transportation has
painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

㉠
㉡

“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
But just because companies have to provide the
option, it doesn’t mean they have to make it easy
for you to see! So the “unsubscribe” link is made
almost ⓑ[invisible / invisibly] in the email. Gray
print on a dark background is rather hard to read,
as is very small print.
Dark
patterns
are
everywhere.
It
is
always
important to be aware ⓒ[that / what] a company’s
goals don’t always correspond with your own. To
detect and resist dark patterns, you need to read
carefully and think before you click on a button.

Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark

Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark pattern
ⓒwhere your credit card is automatically charged as
soon as a free trial comes to an end. While the
companies that ⓓdoing this would argue that it
enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning ⓔwhich
their cards are about to be charged, often causing
them ⓕto be billed unexpectedly. This method is

body:
Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that
companies
use
to
manipulate
consumer
behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.

습니다. A few moments later, Eugenio Arias, a man

the limousine. Despite the fact that Picasso was

had] been close friends for twenty years. Let’s go back
to that summer afternoon (C)[which / when] their

(C)

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두골라 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓑ feeling → feel (made와 목적어 Picasso에 이어져 ‘make+ 목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이며, Picasso가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이고, 사역동사 make의 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 경우 목적격보어 로 동사원형을 사용하므로, feeling을 동사원형 feel로 고친다.) ⓓ more strongly → stronger (‘~되다’라는 뜻의 2형식 동사 grow의 과 거형 grew에 이어진 보어 자리이며, 보어로 부사(구)는 쓸 수 없으므로, 부사의 비교급 more strongly를 형용사의 비교급 stronger로 고친다.) ⓕ preparing → prepared (관계부사 where가 이끄는 절의 동사로 enjoyed가 있으므로, 목적어로 이어진 명사구 Spanish dishes 뒤에 이를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사가 쓰이는 것은 적절하나, 수 식받는 명사구가 ‘준비된’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 행위 주체가 ‘by+명사구’ 형태로 이어져 있으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 preparing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 prepared로 고친다.)

into the limousine. Despite the fact that Picasso was
twenty-eight years older than Arias, the two had
been close friends for twenty years. Let’s go back

_______________________________________________________.

anyone who possessed his hair or nails would have
control over him. ⓓToo superstitious to let other

and entered Arias’s barbershop because he was so
eager
to
meet
his
fellow
countryman.
Arias

As time passed, Picasso’s health (A)[recovered
declined] with age. One day, Picasso asked Arias,
“What are you going to do with all the paintings
and sketches I gave you?” Arias responded that he
would build a museum in Spain to display the
works. Picasso was moved to hear that and swore
to help Arias. But unfortunately, he did not live to
see the museum completed, passing away in 1973.
Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in
knowing that his best friend would live on through
his art. A few years later, Arias returned to Spain
and exhibited Picasso’s works. This small exhibit
attracted visitors from all over the world. A foreign
merchant approached Arias one day and attempted
to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works. But
he (B)[refused / consented] to bargain, saying, “Even
if you bring all the money in your country, I will
not sell any of his works to you. His works are
symbols of the friendship between Picasso and me.”
The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio Arias (The
Picasso Museum - Eugenio Arias Collection) was
finally completed. This was possible because Arias
donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso’s
works to Arias’s hometown of Buitrago del Lozoya.
They comprised a collection of paintings, posters,
ceramics, and other works. Each of them is
(C)[indistinguishable / distinct] from Picasso’s other
works because Picasso carved each one with the
inscription Para mi amigo, Arias (For my friend,
Arias). When visitors enter this museum, they
quickly discover that it is more than just a tribute
to honor Picasso’s artistic legacy; it is also a
monument to the artist and barber’s lifelong
friendship.

body:
Can monkeys be friends with horses? How about giraffes and goats? It seems that animals of different species are not compatible with one another, but there is one special friendship that bloomed between a dog and a dolphin. The close friendship between Gunner, a seven-year-old dog, and Delta, a ten-year-old dolphin, is an extraordinary bond that goes beyond the boundaries of their species. Despite their differences in habitat, Gunner and Delta have formed a deep and genuine connection that shows the beauty of friendship between different species. Their first encounter occurred when Gunner’s owner took him to the Dolphin Research Center where Delta lives. As Gunner observed Delta swimming elegantly in the water, he could not help but be fascinated by the dolphin’s grace and friendliness. Gunner, with his playful and loyal nature, seemed to be initially intrigued by Delta’s graceful movements and intelligent behavior. Gunner approached the edge of the enclosure and walked alongside the water while wagging his tail, his tongue hanging out in excitement. Delta, being an exceptionally clever creature, sensed Gunner’s friendly intentions and politely swam over to meet him. The two animals inspected each other with cautious sniffs and gentle touches, quickly establishing a sense of trust. Gunner and Delta would have fun together, engaging in playful games. For example, Gunner would bounce around and chase Delta’s splashes, and Delta would perform leaps for Gunner’s amusement. Their interactions were a harmonious dance of joy and companionship, breaking the barriers of their different physical abilities.

choices: How Different Habitats Shape Animal Behavior
How We Interpret Friendships Between Different Species
Touching: The Language of Trust Among Animals
Building Friendship and Trust: An Instinct for Survival
The Beauty of Friendship Beyond Biological Boundaries

body:
How much time do you spend sitting per day?
Studies have found that one-third of the global
population aged fifteen years and older engage in
insufficient physical activity. (A)특히, 청소년들은 앉아
있는 데 너무 많은 시간을 보내고 정기적으로 활동적
인 신체 활동에 거의 참여하지 않습니다.
The scientific community has even coined the term
“sitting disease” for this phenomenon in order to
represent the harmful health effects that result from long
periods of sitting. The longer you sit, the more exposed
you are to the dangers of obesity, heart disease,
diabetes, and even depression. Walking, according to
health experts, is one of the safest, easiest, and cheapest
forms of exercise to combat sitting disease.

choices: Physical Activity Guidelines for Teenagers
Why Teenagers Prefer Sitting Over Exercising
Causes and Treatments of Depression in Adolescents

solution: 전 세계 15세 이상 인구의 3분의 1이 신체 활동이 부족하며 특히, 청소년들은 너무 오래 앉아 있어 신체 활동을 거의 하지 않는데, 이렇게 오래 앉아 있는 것으로 인한 현상을 일컫는 ‘sitting disease(의자병)’라는 용어를 소개하고, 이로 인해 노출 되는 건강상의 위험(비만, 심장병, 당뇨병, 우울증)과 방지책인 걷기 운동을 제안하는 글이므로, 글의 제목으로 ❹ ‘장시간 앉 아 있는 것의 문제점들과 그 해결책들’이 알맞다.

solution: (A) 앞에서 친구와 함께 걷기로 계획할 때, 여러분은 여러분의 친 구를 실망시키고 싶지 않기 때문에 걷기를 완수할 가능성이 더 높 다는 내용이 왔고 (A) 뒤에서는 대화를 나눌 누군가가 있는 것은 여러분이 운동하고 있다는 사실을 잊고 시간이 순식간에 지나가게 만든다는 내용으로 걷기를 더 잘 할 수 있는 방법이 추가되므로, (A)에는 ‘게다가’를 뜻하는 접속사 Besides, Additionally가 알맞다. body:
Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking (A)______________________________? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: can help lower your cravings for sugary foods
can increase your appetite for sweet snacks like chocolate
can lower your blood pressure almost as much as running
can strengthen your bones just as effectively as dairy products
can help support your immune system and reduce the need for medicine

2. 따라서 빈칸에는 걷기가 ‘단 음식에 대한 갈망을 낮추는 데 도움이 된다’는 말이 와야 한다.

4. 따라서 답은 ①이다.

the connection between walking and enhanced creativity
the role of brain areas responsible for learning and memory

body:
Walking is not only a simple way to avoid the harmful effects of sitting disease, but it also has other health benefits. You may already be aware of the health benefits of walking, such as bone strengthening, blood pressure reduction, and improved heart health. But did you know that walking can help lower your cravings for sugary foods? According to research by the University of Exeter, taking daily walks for fifteen minutes can cut chocolate consumption in half. This is because frequent physical activity can enhance brain function, making it easier to limit our consumption of sweet foods such as chocolate. Moreover, walking can keep you from getting sick during the cold and flu season. A study found that people who walked for at least twenty minutes a day, five days a week, had 43% fewer sick days than those who exercised once a week or less. And even if they did get sick, it was for a shorter period of time with milder symptoms. This is primarily due to the improved immune system that results from walking regularly.

choices: Why Chocolate Cravings Are Hard to Control
How to Reduce Sugar Cravings Without Exercise
How the University of Exeter Conducts Health Research
Surprising Health Benefits of Walking Beyond the Basics
The Link Between Exercise Frequency and the Immune System

the beauty of your surroundings with, ⓕmaking your
walks more exciting and engaging.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Having a walking buddy can encourage you togo for a walk, especially when you feel lonelyor bored with walking alone.
People tend to follow through with walkingplans made with a friend because they do notwant to disappoint their friend.
Chatting with a friend while walking can makethe time seem to pass faster.
Having a talk while walking can make youforget how far you have walked.
Walking alone allows you to enjoy the beautyof your surroundings more fully than walkingwith a friend does.
solution: 친구와 함께 걸으면 주변의 아름다움을 공유할 수 있는 누군 가를 두는 것이라고 했으므로, ❺ ‘친구와 함께 걷는 것보다 혼자 걷는 것은 주변의 아름다움을 더 충분히 즐길 수 있게 해 준다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 전체의 중심 내용을 담은 주제문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

ⓐ Reading slowly and carefully is one of the most valuable skills a student can develop in an age of endless information. ⓑ Online, we are trained to skim: our eyes jump from headline to headline, and we rarely stay with one text for more than a few minutes. ⓒ This habit may help us gather facts quickly, but it leaves little room for the kind of thinking that turns information into understanding. ⓓ When we read slowly, we have time to question the author's claims, connect new ideas to what we already know, and notice what has been left unsaid. ⓔ Deep reading also strengthens our ability to concentrate, an ability that is increasingly rare and therefore increasingly precious. Of course, skimming has its place; no one needs to study a bus schedule line by line. But when a text deserves our attention, giving it that attention is not a waste of time. It is the very process through which knowledge becomes our own.
solution:
1. ⓐ 「끝없는 정보의 시대에 천천히 주의 깊게 읽는 것은 학생이 기를 수 있는 가장 가치 있는 기술 중 하나이다.」 — 글 전체의 중심 내용을 첫 문장에서 먼저 제시한다.
2. ⓑ·ⓒ는 훑어 읽기 습관의 한계(정보를 이해로 바꾸는 사고의 여지가 없음), ⓓ·ⓔ는 천천히 읽을 때의 이점(주장 검토·지식 연결, 집중력 강화)으로 ⓐ를 뒷받침한다. 마지막 문장 「그것이 바로 지식이 우리 자신의 것이 되는 과정이다」도 ⓐ를 다시 확인한다.
3. 대표 오답 ⓔ는 깊이 읽기의 여러 이점 가운데 «집중력» 하나만 말한 세부 근거이므로 주제문이 될 수 없다.
4. 따라서 답은 ①이다.

body:
다음 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 전체의 중심 내용을 담은 주제문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

In school, a wrong answer is usually marked with a red X and quickly forgotten. ⓐ In a laboratory, however, a failed experiment is rarely thrown away so easily. ⓑ When a result does not match the prediction, a careful scientist asks why, because the gap between what was expected and what actually happened often points to something no one has noticed before. ⓒ Many important discoveries began in exactly this way, as an annoying result that refused to go away. ⓓ Even when a failure reveals nothing new, it tells researchers which paths are not worth following, saving others from repeating the same mistake. ⓔ In science, then, failure is not the opposite of progress but one of its most important sources of information. Students might benefit from adopting a similar attitude. Instead of hiding their mistakes, they could study them, asking what each error reveals about their understanding. A wrong answer examined honestly can teach more than a right answer reached by luck.
solution:
1. ⓔ 「그렇다면 과학에서 실패는 진보의 반대가 아니라 진보의 가장 중요한 정보원 중 하나이다.」 — then(그렇다면)으로 앞의 내용을 일반화해 글의 중심 내용을 정리한다.
2. ⓐ 실험실에서는 실패를 쉽게 버리지 않음 → ⓑ 예측과 결과의 차이가 새로운 것을 가리킴 → ⓒ 중요한 발견이 그렇게 시작됨 → ⓓ 아무것도 드러나지 않아도 가지 말아야 할 길을 알려 줌 — 모두 ⓔ의 근거이다. 마지막 세 문장은 이를 학생의 태도에 적용한 것이다.
